title.zh: 卷四百〇二 列傳第一百六十一 陳敏 張詔 畢再遇 安丙 楊巨源 李好義
title.en: Volume 402 Biographies 161: Chen Min, Zhang Zhao, Bi Zaiyu, An Bing, Yang Juyuan, Li Haoyi
title.raw: 卷四百〇二 列傳第一百六十一 陳敏 張詔 畢再遇 安丙 楊巨源 李好義 Volume 402 Biographies 161: Chen Min, Zhang Zhao, Bi Zaiyu, An Bing, Yang Juyuan, Li Haoyi

sentences.zh: 陳敏，字元功，贛之石城人。

translations.literal: Chen Min, style name Yuangong, was a native of Shicheng in Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min, courtesy name Yuangong, was from Shicheng in Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 父皓，有才武，建炎末，以破贛賊李仁功，補官至承信郎。

translations.literal: His father Hao had talent in civil and military affairs; at the end of the Jianyan era, for defeating the Gan bandit Li Rengong, he was rewarded with appointment to the rank of Chengxin Lang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen Hao was skilled in both civil and military affairs; late in the Jianyan reign he crushed the Ganzhou rebel Li Rengong and was promoted to the rank of Chengxin Lang.

sentences.zh: 敏身長六尺餘，精騎射，積官至忠靖郎。

translations.literal: Min's body height was over six chi; he excelled at mounted archery and through accumulated promotions reached the post of Zhongjing Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Min stood over six feet tall, excelled in horsemanship and archery, and rose through the ranks to Zhongjing Lang.

sentences.zh: 以楊存中薦，擢閤門祗候。

translations.literal: On Yang Cunzhong's recommendation, he was promoted to Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Yang Cunzhong, he was appointed Gate Attendant at the imperial gate.

sentences.zh: 時閩地多寇，殿司兵往戍，率不習水土。

translations.literal: At that time Fujian had many bandits; when Palace Division troops went to garrison there, they generally did not acclimate to the water and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was then rife with bandits, but Palace Division troops sent to garrison the region usually could not adjust to the local climate.

sentences.zh: 至是，始募三千兵置左翼軍，以敏為統制，漳州駐紮。

translations.literal: At this time they first recruited three thousand troops to establish the Left Wing Army, with Min as commander, stationed at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court then recruited three thousand men to form the Left Wing Army, appointing Min as its commander with headquarters at Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敏按諸郡要害，凡十有三處，悉分兵扼之，盜發輒獲。

translations.literal: Min surveyed the strategic points of the various prefectures—there were thirteen in all—and deployed troops to hold each; whenever bandits struck they were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Min mapped the strategic choke points across the prefectures—thirteen in all—and posted troops at each; bandits were captured whenever they struck.

sentences.zh: 贛州齊述據城叛，嘯聚數萬，將棄城南寇。

translations.literal: Qi Shu of Ganzhou seized the city in rebellion, mustering tens of thousands, and was about to abandon the city and raid southward.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shu of Ganzhou seized the city in revolt, rallied tens of thousands of followers, and was preparing to abandon the city and raid south.

sentences.zh: 敏聞之曰：「贛兵精勁，善走嶮，若朝廷發兵未至，萬一奔衝，江、湖、閩、廣騷動矣。」

translations.literal: When Min heard this he said: "Ganzhou troops are crack soldiers, skilled at rushing rugged terrain; if court troops have not yet arrived and they should break out and charge, Jiang, Hu, Min, and Guang will all be thrown into turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: When Min heard the news he said, "Ganzhou troops are crack fighters who excel on difficult terrain; if imperial forces have not yet arrived and the rebels break out, the Yangzi region, Hunan, Fujian, and Guangdong will all be thrown into chaos."

sentences.zh: 不俟命，領所部馳七日，徑抵贛圍其城。

translations.literal: Without awaiting orders, he led his command and rode hard for seven days, going straight to Ganzhou and besieging the city.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for orders, he led his troops on a seven-day forced march straight to Ganzhou and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 逾月，朝廷命李耕以諸路兵至，破之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the court ordered Li Geng to come with troops from the various circuits and break them.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the court dispatched Li Geng with troops from several circuits, and the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 累功授右武大夫，封武功縣男，領興州刺史。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was appointed Right Martial Grandee, enfeoffed as Baron of Wugong, and given concurrent charge as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated merit he was appointed Right Martial Grandee, ennobled as Baron of Wugong, and made prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，高宗見其狀貌魁岸，除破敵軍統制。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, Gaozong saw his imposing stature and made him commander of the Enemy-Breaking Army.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, Emperor Gaozong was struck by his imposing bearing and appointed him commander of the Enemy-Breaking Army.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，詔起復，以所部駐太平州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; an edict recalled him from mourning, and he stationed his troops at Taipingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother, but an edict recalled him from filial leave and he stationed his command at Taipingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，金主亮來攻，成閔為京湖路招討使，以敏軍隸之，升馬司統制，軍於荊、漢間。

translations.literal: In the 31st year of Shaoxing the Jin ruler Liang came to attack; Cheng Min became commissioner for the Jing-Hu circuit, Min's army was placed under him, he was promoted to Horse Division commander-in-chief, with troops between Jing and Han.
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, when the Jin emperor Hailing launched his invasion, Cheng Min was made commissioner for the Jing-Hu circuit; Min's forces were placed under his command, Min was promoted to commander-in-chief of the Horse Division, and camped between Jingzhou and the Han River.

sentences.zh: 敏說閔曰：「金人精騎悉在淮，汴都必無守備，若由陳、蔡徑搗大梁，潰其腹心，此救江、淮之術也。」

translations.literal: Min urged Cheng Min, saying: "The Jin crack cavalry are all on the Huai; Bianjing surely has no defense. If we strike Da Liang straight through Chen and Cai, rupturing their core, this is the way to save Jiang and Huai."
translations.idiomatic: Min urged Cheng Min: "All the Jin elite cavalry are on the Huai front; Kaifeng must be undefended. If we strike straight through Chen and Cai to hit Kaifeng and rupture their heartland, that is how we relieve the Yangzi and Huai regions."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Min would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 從閔還駐廣陵，時金兵尚未渡淮，敏又說閔邀其歸師，復不聽。

translations.literal: Following Min back to garrison Guangling—at that time Jin troops had not yet crossed the Huai—Min again urged Min to intercept their returning columns, and again he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Min withdrew to Guangling, the Jin had not yet crossed the Huai; Min again urged him to intercept their retreating columns, and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 敏遂移疾歸姑孰。

translations.literal: Min then cited illness and returned to Guzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Min then pleaded illness and retired to Guzhu.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，張浚宣撫江、淮，奏敏為神勁軍統制。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, Zhang Jun was commissioner for Jiang-Huai and recommended Min as commander of the Shenjin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Zhang Jun was made commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region and recommended Min as commander of the Shenjin Army.

sentences.zh: 浚視師，改都督府武鋒軍都統制。

translations.literal: When Jun went to inspect the armies, Min was changed to commander-in-chief of the Wufeng Army in the Commander-in-Chief's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun went to inspect the armies in person, Min was made commander-in-chief of the Wufeng Army under the Commander-in-Chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣李顯忠北伐，浚欲以敏偕行，敏曰：「盛夏興師非時，且金人重兵皆在大梁，我客彼主，勝負之勢先形矣。

translations.literal: The court sent Li Xianzhong on a northern expedition; Jun wished Min to go with him. Min said: "Launching armies in midsummer is ill-timed; moreover the Jin heavy forces are all at Da Liang—we are guests, they hosts; the pattern of victory and defeat is already shaped.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Li Xianzhong on a northern expedition, and Zhang Jun wanted Min to accompany him. Min objected: "Launching a campaign in midsummer is ill-timed, and the Jin main forces are all at Kaifeng—we would be invaders on their ground, and the odds are already against us.

sentences.zh: 願少緩。」

translations.literal: I beg a slight delay."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the campaign be postponed a little longer."

sentences.zh: 浚不聽，令敏屯盱眙。

translations.literal: Jun did not listen and ordered Min to garrison at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun would not listen and ordered Min to garrison at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 顯忠至符離，果失律，敏遂入泗州守之。

translations.literal: Xianzhong reached Fuli and indeed violated regulations; Min then entered Sizhou to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong reached Fuli he indeed broke discipline; Min then entered Sizhou to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 金人議和，詔敏退守滁陽。

translations.literal: The Jin sought peace; an edict ordered Min to withdraw and garrison Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin sought peace, an edict ordered Min to withdraw and garrison Chuyang.

sentences.zh: 敏請於朝，謂滁非受敵之所，改戍高郵，兼知軍事。

translations.literal: Min petitioned the court, saying Chuzhou was not a place to receive the enemy, and was reassigned to garrison Gaoyou, with concurrent military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Min petitioned the court, arguing that Chuzhou was unsuited to meeting the enemy head-on, and was reassigned to garrison Gaoyou with concurrent charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 與金人戰射陽湖，敗之，焚其舟，追至沛城，復敗之。

translations.literal: Fighting the Jin at Sheyang Lake he defeated them, burned their boats, pursued to Peicheng, and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Jin at Sheyang Lake, routed them, burned their boats, pursued them to Peicheng, and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 四年，北界人侍旺叛於漣水軍，密款本朝，稱結約山東十二州豪傑起義，以復中原。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shi Wang, a man from the northern frontier, rebelled at the Lianshui army, secretly treating with our court, claiming to have allied twelve prefectures of Shandong's worthies to rise and recover the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shi Wang, a man from the Jin frontier, rebelled at the Lianshui garrison and secretly pledged allegiance to the Song, claiming he had rallied the leading men of twelve Shandong prefectures to rise and recover the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 上以問敏，敏曰：「旺欲假吾國威以行劫爾，必不能成事，願勿聽。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Min, who said: "Wang merely wishes to borrow our state's prestige to raid and plunder—he certainly cannot succeed; I beg you not heed him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Min, who replied, "Wang only wants to borrow our prestige to raid and plunder—he cannot possibly succeed. I beg Your Majesty not to heed him."

sentences.zh: 適屯田統領官與旺交通，旺敗，金有間言，上知非敏罪，乃召敏為左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Just then an officer of the farming-administration command had dealings with Wang; Wang was defeated, the Jin spread suspicious talk, the emperor knew it was not Min's fault, and summoned Min as General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a farming-administration commander was found to have been in contact with Wang; when Wang was defeated the Jin spread rumors of collusion, but the emperor knew Min was innocent and summoned him to court as General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 言事者議欲戍守清河口，敏言：「金兵每出清河，必遣人馬先自上流潛渡，今欲必守其地，宜先修楚州城池，蓋楚州為南北襟喉，彼此必爭之地。

translations.literal: Memorialists debated garrisoning the Qinghe mouth; Min said: "Whenever Jin troops come out on the Qinghe they always send men and horses first to ford secretly upstream; if we mean to hold that place firmly we should first repair Chuzhou's walls and moat—for Chuzhou is the strategic throat between north and south, a place both sides must contest.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists debated garrisoning the mouth of the Qinghe River; Min argued, "Whenever Jin forces advance along the Qinghe they first send detachments to ford secretly upstream. If we mean to hold that position firmly we must first repair the walls of Chuzhou, for Chuzhou is the strategic throat between north and south—a place both sides are bound to fight over.

sentences.zh: 長淮二千餘里，河道通北方者五，清、汴、渦、潁、蔡是也；

translations.literal: The Long Huai exceeds two thousand li; rivers communicating with the north number five—Qing, Bian, Wo, Ying, and Cai;
translations.idiomatic: The Long Huai stretches more than two thousand li; five waterways connect it to the north—the Qinghe, Bian River, Wo River, Ying River, and Cai River;

sentences.zh: 通南方以入江者，惟楚州運河耳。

translations.literal: those entering the Yangtze from the south have only the Chuzhou canal.
translations.idiomatic: and the only route from the south into the Yangtze is the Chuzhou canal.

sentences.zh: 北人舟艦自五河而下，將謀渡江，非得楚州運河，無緣自達。

translations.literal: Northern boats coming down the five rivers will seek to cross the Yangtze; without the Chuzhou canal they have no channel to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: When northern fleets come down those five rivers intending to cross the Yangtze, they cannot reach the river without control of the Chuzhou canal.

sentences.zh: 昔周世宗自楚州北神堰鑿老鸛河，通戰艦以入大江，南唐遂失兩淮之地。

translations.literal: Of old Emperor Shizong of Zhou from Chuzhou's north Shenyan cut the Laoguan River, connecting war vessels to enter the Great River, and Southern Tang thereby lost the land between the two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou cut the Laoguan River from the north Shenyan dam at Chuzhou so that warships could reach the Yangtze, and Southern Tang thereby lost the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，楚州實為南朝司命，願朝廷留意。」

translations.literal: From this it may be said Chuzhou is truly the lifeline of the Southern dynasty—I beg the court take note."
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that Chuzhou is truly the lifeline of the Southern dynasty; I beg the court to take heed."

sentences.zh: 及是，再出守高郵，乃詔與楚州守臣左祐同城楚州，祐卒，遂移守楚州。

translations.literal: At this time he went out again to guard Gaoyou; then an edict ordered him to share Chuzhou with defender Zuo You; when You died he moved to hold Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he was again posted to guard Gaoyou; then an edict ordered him to share command of Chuzhou with the defender Zuo You, and when You died he took sole charge of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 北使過者觀其雉堞堅新，號「銀鑄城」。

translations.literal: Northern envoys who passed looked at its fresh, sturdy ramparts and called it the "silver-cast city."
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys who passed through marveled at its fresh, sturdy ramparts and called it the "Silver-Cast City."

sentences.zh: 以歸正人二百家逃歸，降授忠州團練使，罷為福建路總管，改江西路總管，贛州駐劄。

translations.literal: Because two hundred surrendered households fled back, he was demoted to regiment commander of Zhongzhou, dismissed to circuit commander of Fujian, then changed to Jiangxi circuit commander, stationed at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When two hundred surrendered households fled back to the Jin he was demoted to regiment commander of Zhongzhou, relieved as Fujian circuit commander, reassigned as Jiangxi circuit commander, and stationed at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，朝廷命往福州揀軍，又命還豫章教閱江西團結諸郡人馬。

translations.literal: After a month plus the court ordered him to Fuzhou to select troops, then ordered him back to Yuzhang to drill the Jiangxi muster troops of the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month the court ordered him to Fuzhou to select troops, then back to Yuzhang to drill the Jiangxi militia levies from the various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俄提舉佑神觀，仍奉朝請，繼復蘄州防禦使，再除武鋒軍都統制兼知楚州，復光州觀察使，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was made director of the Youshen Temple and court gentleman; again made defense commissioner of Qizhou, again commander-in-chief of Wufeng with concurrent prefect of Chuzhou, restored observer of Guangzhou, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the Youshen Temple while retaining his court-gentleman status; he was again made defense commissioner of Qizhou, again commander-in-chief of the Wufeng Army with concurrent prefect of Chuzhou, restored to observer of Guangzhou, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 特贈慶遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded military commissioner of Qingyuan army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the rank of military commissioner of the Qingyuan army.

sentences.zh: 張詔，字君卿，成州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, style name Junqing, was a native of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Junqing, was from Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 少隸張浚帳下，積功守和州。

translations.literal: In youth he served under Zhang Jun's command and through merit became defender of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served under Zhang Jun and through accumulated merit became defender of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗被旨介聘，一日金人持所繪祐、獻二陵像至館中，皆北地服，詔向之再拜。

translations.literal: Once entrusted on an embassy, one day Jin men brought painted portraits of the You and Xian mausoleums to the hostel—all in northern dress; Zhao bowed twice toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Once sent on an embassy, he was one day shown portraits of the You and Xian imperial mausoleums painted by the Jin—all figures in northern dress—and Zhao bowed twice toward them.

sentences.zh: 館者問之，答曰：「詔雖不識其人，但龍鳳之姿，天日之表，疑非北朝祖宗也，敢不拜！」

translations.literal: The hostel staff asked him; he answered: "Though Zhao does not recognize the persons, their dragon-phoenix bearing, sun-and-moon visage—I doubt they are ancestors of the northern court—how dare I not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: When the hostel staff questioned him he replied, "Though I do not know who these figures are, their bearing is that of dragon and phoenix, their visage like sun and moon—I doubt they are ancestors of the northern court. How could I not bow!"

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞而喜之，由是驟用。

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard and was pleased, and from this he was rapidly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong heard of this he was delighted, and from that moment Zhao was rapidly promoted.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，除興州都統制兼知興州，代吳挺。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he was made commander-in-chief of Xingzhou with concurrent prefect of Xingzhou, replacing Wu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1194 he was appointed commander-in-chief of Xingzhou with concurrent prefect of Xingzhou, replacing Wu Ting.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，趙彥逾帥蜀，以關外去興元遠，緩急恐失事機，復請分東西為二帥，詔遂兼西路安撫司公事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan Zhao Yanyu commanded Shu; because territory beyond the pass was far from Xingyuan and urgent matters might miss their moment, he again asked to split east and west into two commanders; an edict thereupon had Zhao also handle affairs of the western-route pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1196 Zhao Yanyu took command of Shu; because the territory beyond the pass was far from Xingyuan and emergencies might miss their moment, he again petitioned to split the command into eastern and western wings, and an edict had Zhao also handle affairs of the western-route pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，趙汝愚為從官時，每奏吳氏世掌蜀兵，非國家之利，請以張詔代領武興之軍。

translations.literal: Earlier when Zhao Ruyu was an attendant official he repeatedly memorialized that the Wu clan had held Shu troops for generations—not in the state's interest—and asked that Zhang Zhao replace command of the Wuxing army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhao Ruyu was an attendant official, he had repeatedly memorialized that the Wu clan's hereditary control of Shu troops was not in the state's interest and asked that Zhang Zhao replace them in command of the Wuxing army.

sentences.zh: 蓋汝愚之意欲以吳曦為文臣帥，以杜他日握兵之漸，而未及行也。

translations.literal: Ruyu's intent was to make Wu Xi a civil commander, to cut off the gradual grasp of military power, but this had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu's intent was to install Wu Xi as a civil commander in order to forestall a future military monopoly, but this plan had not yet been carried out.

sentences.zh: 汝愚既知樞密院，力辭不拜，白於光宗曰：「若武興朝除帥，則臣夕拜命。」

translations.literal: When Ruyu came to know the Bureau of Military Affairs he strongly declined the appointment, telling Guangzong: "If Wuxing gets a court-appointed commander in the morning, I shall accept the post that evening."
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs he firmly declined the post, telling Emperor Guangzong, "If a court-appointed commander is named for Wuxing in the morning, I shall accept my commission that same evening."

sentences.zh: 上許之，乃以詔為成州團練使、興州諸軍都統制。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, and Zhao was made regiment commander of Chengzhou and commander-in-chief of all Xingzhou forces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Zhao was made regiment commander of Chengzhou and commander-in-chief of all Xingzhou forces.

sentences.zh: 詔在興州，甚得士心。

translations.literal: Zhao at Xingzhou won the troops' hearts deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingzhou Zhao won the deep loyalty of his troops.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，郭杲代之。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year; Guo Guo replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Qingyuan; Guo Guo replaced him.

sentences.zh: 畢再遇

translations.literal: Bi Zaiyu
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zaiyu

sentences.zh: 畢再遇，字德卿，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Bi Zaiyu, style name Deqing, was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zaiyu, courtesy name Deqing, was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父進，建炎間從岳飛護衛八陵，轉戰江、淮間，積階至武義大夫。

translations.literal: His father Jin, in the Jianyan era followed Yue Fei guarding the Eight Mausoleums, fought between Jiang and Huai, rising to Martial Righteousness Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi Jin, during the Jianyan era, followed Yue Fei in guarding the Eight Imperial Mausoleums and fought across the Jiang-Huai region, rising to the rank of Martial Righteousness Grandee.

sentences.zh: 再遇以恩補官，隸侍衛馬司，武藝絕人，挽弓至二石七斗，背挽一石八斗，步射二石，馬射一石五斗。

translations.literal: Zaiyu received office by grace, served in the Palace Horse Division; his martial skill was peerless—drawing the bow to 2.7 shi, drawing backward 1.8 shi, shooting 2 shi on foot, 1.5 shi mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu received office by hereditary privilege and served in the Palace Horse Division; his martial skill was unmatched—he could draw a bow to 2.7 shi, draw backward to 1.8 shi, shoot 2 shi on foot, and 1.5 shi from horseback.

sentences.zh: 孝宗召見，太悅，賜戰袍、金錢。

translations.literal: Xiaozong summoned him, was greatly pleased, and gave battle robes and gold cash.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong summoned him to court, was greatly pleased, and bestowed battle robes and gold cash.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，下詔北伐，以殿帥郭倪招撫山東、京東，遣再遇與統制陳孝慶取泗州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi an edict launched the northern campaign; Palace Commander Guo Ni was commissioner for Shandong and Jingdong, sending Zaiyu with commander Chen Xiaoqing to take Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1206 an edict launched the northern campaign; Palace Commander Guo Ni was made commissioner for Shandong and Jingdong and sent Zaiyu with the commander Chen Xiaoqing to take Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 再遇請選新刺敢死軍為前鋒，倪以八十七人付之。

translations.literal: Zaiyu asked to select freshly drafted dare-death troops as vanguard; Ni gave him eighty-seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu asked to select freshly drafted dare-to-die troops as his vanguard; Ni gave him eighty-seven men.

sentences.zh: 招撫司克日進兵，金人聞之，閉榷場、塞城門為備。

translations.literal: The pacification office set a day to advance; the Jin heard and closed the market gates and barricaded the city gates in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification office set a fixed day for the advance; when the Jin heard of it they closed the market and sealed the city gates in preparation.

sentences.zh: 再遇曰：「敵已知吾濟師之日矣，兵以奇勝，當先一日出其不意。」

translations.literal: Zaiyu said: "The foe already knows our crossing day—victory lies in surprise; we should go one day earlier unexpectedly."
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu said, "The enemy already knows the day we plan to cross—victory lies in surprise; we should advance one day early and catch them off guard."

sentences.zh: 孝慶從之。

translations.literal: Xiaoqing followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing agreed.

sentences.zh: 再遇饗士卒，激以忠義，進兵薄泗州。

translations.literal: Zaiyu feasted the troops, stirred them with loyalty and righteousness, and advanced pressing on Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu feasted his troops and roused them with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, then advanced to press on Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 泗有東西兩城，再遇令陳戈旗舟楫於石屯下，如欲攻西城者，乃自以麾下兵從陟山徑趨東城南角，先登，殺敵數百，金人大潰，守城者開北門遁。

translations.literal: Sizhou had east and west cities; Zaiyu had Chen set flags and boats at Shitun as if to attack the west city, then himself with his troops climbed the mountain path straight at the southeast corner of the east city, mounting first, killing several hundred; the Jin routed in great numbers; defenders opened the north gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou had eastern and western cities. Zaiyu had Chen display banners and boats at Shitun as if preparing to attack the west city, while he himself led his troops up the mountain path straight to the southeast corner of the east city, scaling the walls first and killing several hundred Jin soldiers; the Jin forces routed in panic and the defenders fled through the north gate.

sentences.zh: 西城猶堅守，再遇立大將旗，呼曰：「大宋畢將軍在此，爾等中原遺民也，可速降。」

translations.literal: The west city still held firm; Zaiyu raised the great general's flag and shouted: "Great Song General Bi is here—you are remnant people of the Central Plain, submit at once!"
translations.idiomatic: The west city still held out. Zaiyu raised his commander's banner and shouted, "General Bi of Great Song is here! You are people of the Central Plain—surrender at once!"

sentences.zh: 旋有淮平知縣縋城而下乞降，於是兩城皆定。

translations.literal: Soon the Huai-ping county magistrate let himself down by rope begging surrender, and thus both cities were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the magistrate of Huaiping county let himself down by rope to beg surrender, and both cities were secured.

sentences.zh: 郭倪來饗士，出御寶刺史牙牌授再遇，辭曰：「國家河南八十有一州，今下泗兩城即得一刺史，繼此何以賞之？

translations.literal: Guo Ni came to feast the troops and brought out the imperial treasure—the prefect's tally-plaque—to give Zaiyu; he declined: "Our state has eighty-one prefectures south of the River—now taking two cities of Si we get one prefect—how shall we reward after this?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ni came to feast the troops and produced the imperial tally-plaque of a prefect to award Zaiyu, who declined: "The state has eighty-one prefectures south of the River—if we grant a prefect's rank for taking two cities of Sizhou, how shall we reward what comes next?

sentences.zh: 且招撫得朝廷幾牙牌來？」

translations.literal: Moreover, how many tally-plaques has the pacification office received from court?"
translations.idiomatic: And how many tally-plaques has the pacification office received from the court in the first place?"

sentences.zh: 固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 尋除環衛官。

translations.literal: Soon made a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made a palace guard officer.

sentences.zh: 倪調李汝翼、郭倬取宿州，復遣孝慶等繼之。

translations.literal: Ni transferred Li Ruyi and Guo Zhuo to take Suzhou, again sent Xiaoqing and others to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ni dispatched Li Ruyi and Guo Zhuo to take Suzhou and sent Xiaoqing and others to follow up.

sentences.zh: 命再遇以四百八十騎為先鋒取徐州，至虹，遇郭、李兵裹創旋，問之，則曰：「宿州城下大水，我師不利，統制田俊邁已為敵擒矣。」

translations.literal: He ordered Zaiyu with 480 cavalry as vanguard to take Xuzhou; at Hong he met Guo and Li's troops bandaged returning; asked—they said: "Great flood below Suzhou, our army did poorly, commander Tian Junmai was already captured by the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zaiyu with four hundred eighty cavalry as vanguard to take Xuzhou; at Hong he met Guo and Li's troops returning wounded, and when he asked they said, "Floods below Suzhou city—our army fared badly, and Commander Tian Junmai has already been captured by the enemy."

sentences.zh: 再遇督兵疾趨，次靈壁，遇孝慶駐兵於鳳凰山，將引還，再遇曰：「宿州雖不捷，然兵家勝負不常，豈宜遽自挫！

translations.literal: Zaiyu urged the army on swiftly; at Lingbi he met Xiaoqing halted on Phoenix Mountain about to withdraw; Zaiyu said: "Though Suzhou failed, in war victory and defeat are inconstant—how can we suddenly discourage ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu urged his troops forward at speed; at Lingbi he found Xiaoqing halted on Phoenix Mountain and about to withdraw. Zaiyu said, "Though Suzhou was lost, in war fortune turns—how can we lose heart so quickly!

sentences.zh: 吾奉招撫命取徐州，假道於此，寧死靈壁北門外，不死南門外也。」

translations.literal: I am ordered by the pacification office to take Xuzhou, passing here—I would rather die outside Lingbi's north gate than outside the south gate."
translations.idiomatic: I am under orders from the pacification office to take Xuzhou, passing through here—I would rather die outside Lingbi's north gate than outside its south gate."

sentences.zh: 會倪以書抵孝慶，令班師，再遇曰：「郭、李軍潰，賊必追躡，吾當自禦之。」

translations.literal: Just then Ni sent a letter to Xiaoqing ordering withdrawal; Zaiyu said: "Guo and Li's armies collapsed—the enemy is sure to pursue—we shall face them ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ni sent a letter to Xiaoqing ordering withdrawal. Zaiyu said, "Guo and Li's armies have collapsed—the enemy is sure to pursue—we shall hold them off ourselves."

sentences.zh: 金果以五千餘騎分兩道來，再遇令敢死二十人守靈壁北門，自領兵衝敵陣。

translations.literal: The Jin indeed came with five thousand-odd cavalry in two columns; Zaiyu left twenty dare-death men at Lingbi north gate and led his troops to charge the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin indeed came with more than five thousand cavalry in two columns. Zaiyu left twenty dare-to-die men at Lingbi's north gate and led his troops in a charge against the enemy formation.

sentences.zh: 金人見其旗，呼曰：「畢將軍來也！」

translations.literal: The Jin saw his banner and cried: "General Bi has come!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin saw his banner they cried, "General Bi has come!"

sentences.zh: 遂遁。

translations.literal: Then they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then they fled.

sentences.zh: 再遇手揮雙刀，絕水追擊，殺敵甚眾，甲裳盡赤，逐北三十里。

translations.literal: Zaiyu swung twin swords, crossed the water in pursuit, killing many; armor was all red; pursued north thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu swung his twin swords, crossed the water in pursuit, and killed a great many; his armor was drenched red with blood as he pursued the fleeing enemy thirty li.

sentences.zh: 金將有持雙鐵簡躍馬而前，再遇以左刀格其簡，右刀斫其脅，金將墮馬死。

translations.literal: A Jin officer bearing twin iron maces leaped his horse forward; Zaiyu with his left blade parried the mace, with his right hacked his flank—the Jin officer fell dead from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin officer bearing twin iron maces charged forward on horseback; Zaiyu parried the mace with his left blade and hacked the man's flank with his right—the Jin officer fell dead from his horse.

sentences.zh: 諸軍發靈壁，再遇獨留未動，度軍行二十餘里，乃火靈壁。

translations.literal: The various armies left Lingbi; Zaiyu alone stayed unmoved; when the army had marched twenty-odd li he then burned Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: The main army departed Lingbi while Zaiyu alone remained; when the column had marched more than twenty li he set fire to Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 諸將問：「夜不火，火今日，何也？」

translations.literal: The generals asked: "Why not burn by night but burn today—what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked, "Why not burn at night but burn in broad daylight—what is the reason?"

sentences.zh: 再遇曰：「夜則照見虛實，晝則煙埃莫睹，彼已敗不敢迫，諸軍乃可安行無虞。

translations.literal: Zaiyu said: "By night flames reveal truth and falsehood; by day smoke and dust obscure—he has already lost and dares not press—then the armies can march in peace without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu replied, "At night the flames would reveal our true strength; by day the smoke and dust would hide it. The enemy has already been defeated and dares not press us—the army can march in safety.

sentences.zh: 汝輩安知兵易進而難退邪？」

translations.literal: How would you know war is easy to advance but hard to withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: How would you know that in war it is easy to advance but hard to withdraw?"

sentences.zh: 還泗州，以功第一，自武節郎超授武功大夫，除左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Returning to Sizhou, for top merit he leaped from Military Festival Lang to Martial Merit Grandee, made General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Sizhou he was ranked first in merit, promoted in one leap from Military Festival Lang to Martial Merit Grandee, and made General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 於是丘崈代鄧友龍為宣撫使，檄倪還維揚，尋棄泗州。

translations.literal: Then Qiu Yi replaced Deng Youlong as commissioner; ordered Ni back to Weiyang, soon abandoned Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qiu Yi replaced Deng Youlong as commissioner, ordered Ni back to Yangzhou, and soon abandoned Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 命再遇還盱眙，遂知盱眙軍，尋改鎮江中軍統制，兼守如故。

translations.literal: Ordered Zaiyu back to Xuyi, then made him military prefect of Xuyi, soon changed to commander of Zhenjiang central army, keeping his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu was ordered back to Xuyi and made military prefect of Xuyi; soon he was changed to commander of the Zhenjiang central army while retaining his defensive duties.

sentences.zh: 以鳳凰山功，授達州刺史。

translations.literal: For Phoenix Mountain merit he was made prefect of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit at Phoenix Mountain he was made prefect of Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬，金人以騎步數萬、戰船五百餘艘渡淮，泊楚州、淮陰間，宣撫司檄再遇援楚，遣段政、張貴代之。

translations.literal: That winter the Jin with tens of thousands cavalry and infantry and five hundred-odd war vessels crossed the Huai, anchored between Chuzhou and Huaiyin; the pacification office ordered Zaiyu to aid Chu, sent Duan Zheng and Zhang Gui to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin crossed the Huai with tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry and more than five hundred warships, anchoring between Chuzhou and Huaiyin; the pacification office ordered Zaiyu to reinforce Chuzhou and sent Duan Zheng and Zhang Gui to replace him at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 再遇既去盱眙，政等驚潰，金人入盱眙；

translations.literal: After Zaiyu left Xuyi, Zheng and the others panicked and collapsed; the Jin entered Xuyi;
translations.idiomatic: After Zaiyu left Xuyi, Zheng and the others panicked and fled; the Jin occupied Xuyi;

sentences.zh: 再遇復定盱眙，除鎮江副都統制。

translations.literal: Zaiyu recovered Xuyi again, made deputy commander-in-chief of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu recovered Xuyi and was made deputy commander-in-chief of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 金兵七萬在楚州城下，三千守淮陰糧，又載糧三千艘泊大清河。

translations.literal: Seventy thousand Jin troops below Chuzhou walls, three thousand guarding Huaiyin grain, another three thousand grain boats anchored on the Great Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy thousand Jin troops were below the walls of Chuzhou, three thousand guarding grain at Huaiyin, and another three thousand grain transports anchored on the Great Qing River.

sentences.zh: 再遇謀知之，曰：「敵眾十倍，難以力勝，可計破也。」

translations.literal: Zaiyu learned this through planning and said: "The enemy are ten times our number—hard to overcome by force; we can plan to break them."
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu learned of this through his scouts and said, "The enemy outnumber us ten to one—we cannot overcome them by force, but we can defeat them by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 乃遣統領許俊間道趨淮陰，夜二鼓銜枚至敵營，各攜火潛入，伏糧車間五十餘所，聞哨聲舉火，敵驚擾奔竄，生擒烏古倫帥勒、蒲察元奴等二十三人。

translations.literal: He then sent commander Xu Jun by a hidden path to Huaiyin; at the second watch of night with gags they reached the enemy camp, each carrying fire sneaking in, hiding among fifty-odd grain wagons; at the signal whistle they lit fires—the enemy panicked and scattered—captured alive Wuguulun Shuile, Pucha Yuannu and twenty-three others.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Commander Xu Jun by a hidden route to Huaiyin; at the second watch his men reached the enemy camp with gags in their mouths, each carrying fire, and hid among more than fifty grain wagons. At the signal whistle they set the fires ablaze; the enemy panicked and fled, and twenty-three men including Wuguulun Shuile and Pucha Yuannu were captured alive.

sentences.zh: 金人復自黃狗灘渡淮，渦口戍將望風遁，濠、滁相繼失守，又破安豐。

translations.literal: The Jin again crossed the Huai at Huanggou Shoals; the Weikou garrison commander fled at the sight of wind; Chuzhou and Hao lost in turn; also broke Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin again crossed the Huai at Huanggou Shoals; the Weikou garrison commander fled without a fight; Hao and Chuzhou fell in succession, and Anfeng was also overrun.

sentences.zh: 再遇謂諸將曰：「楚城堅兵多，敵糧草已空，所慮獨淮西耳。

translations.literal: Zaiyu told the generals: "Chu city is sturdy with many troops; the enemy's grain and fodder are already empty—only Huai west is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyu told his generals, "Chuzhou's walls are strong and its garrison numerous; the enemy's grain and fodder are already exhausted—the only thing to fear is an attack west of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 六合最要害，彼必並力攻之。」

translations.literal: Liuhe is the most vital point; they are certain to combine their strength to attack it."
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe was the key choke point—the enemy would surely throw their full weight against it."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵赴六合。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he led troops to go to Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he marched his army to Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 尋命節制淮東軍馬。

translations.literal: Shortly he was ordered to control and regulate the Huaidong army and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commander over all Huaidong military forces.

sentences.zh: 金人至竹鎮，距六合二十五里。

translations.literal: Jin people arrived at Zhuzhen, twenty-five li from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens reached Zhuzhen, twenty-five li south of Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 再遇登城，偃旗鼓，伏兵南土門，列弩手土城上，敵方臨濠，眾弩俱發，宋師出戰，聞鼓聲，城上旗幟並舉，金人驚遁，追擊大敗之。

translations.literal: Zaiyu ascended the wall, lowered flags and drums, hid troops at the south earthen gate, stationed crossbowmen on the earthen ramparts; when the enemy reached the moat, all crossbows fired together; Song troops sallied forth to fight; hearing the drumbeats, banners on the wall all rose together; Jin people fled in alarm; pursuit inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zaiyu mounted the walls, concealed banners and drums, and posted ambushers at the southern earthen gate with crossbowmen atop the ramparts. When the enemy approached the moat, a volley of bolts swept the field; Song forces sallied out as drums thundered and banners suddenly unfurled along the battlements. The Jurchens panicked and fled; pursuit turned their retreat into a rout.

sentences.zh: 金萬戶完顏蒲辣都、千戶泥龐古等以十萬騎駐成家橋、馬鞍山，進兵圍城數重，欲燒壩木，決壕水，再遇令勁弩射退之。

translations.literal: Jin myriad-household chieftain Wanyan Puladu, thousand-household chieftain Ni Panggu, and others with one hundred thousand cavalry encamped at Chengjia Bridge and Ma'anshan; advancing troops surrounded the city in several rings, intending to burn the dam timber and breach the moat water; Zaiyu ordered powerful crossbows to shoot and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin commanders Wanyan Puladu (wanhu) and Ni Panggu (qianhu), among others, brought a hundred thousand horsemen to camp at Chengjia Bridge and Ma'anshan and tightened the siege ring by ring, planning to burn the dam timbers and breach the moat. Bi Zaiyu ordered his strongest crossbows to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 既而紇石烈都統合兵進攻益急，城中矢盡，再遇令人張青蓋往來城上，金人意其主兵官也，爭射之，須臾矢集樓墻如蝟，獲矢二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hesilie the commander-in-chief combined troops and pressed the attack ever more fiercely; arrows in the city were exhausted; Zaiyu had a person hold a green canopy and walk back and forth on the wall; Jin men took him for their main military officer and vied to shoot at him; in an instant arrows clustered on the tower walls like hedgehog quills; they obtained more than two hundred thousand arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Jin commander Hesilie massed his forces for an even fiercer assault until the city's quiver ran dry. Bi Zaiyu had a soldier stroll the battlements beneath a green canopy; the Jurchens mistook him for the Song commander and showered him with arrows until the parapets bristled like a hedgehog—they recovered more than two hundred thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈引兵退，已乃益增兵，環城四面營帳亙三十里。

translations.literal: Hesilie led troops in withdrawal; afterward he moreover increased troops; encircling the city on four sides, camp tents stretched thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Hesilie drew off, then returned with reinforcements and ringed the city with encampments that stretched thirty li on every side.

sentences.zh: 再遇令臨門作樂以示閑暇，而間出奇兵擊之。

translations.literal: Zaiyu ordered music performed at the gates to show leisure, yet in the intervals sent out strange troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zaiyu had musicians play at the gates to feign ease, while raiding parties struck the enemy camp between assaults.

sentences.zh: 敵晝夜不得休，乃引退。

translations.literal: The enemy obtained no rest day or night; thereupon they led troops in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Denied rest day or night, the enemy finally broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 再遇料其且復來，乃自提兵奪城東野新橋，出敵之背，金人遂遁去，追至滁，大雨雪，乃旋。

translations.literal: Zaiyu estimated they would soon come again; thereupon he himself led troops to seize the wild new bridge east of the city; emerging behind the enemy's back; Jin people then fled away; pursuit reached Chuzhou; heavy rain and snow fell; thereupon they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting the Jurchens to return, Bi Zaiyu led a force to seize the new bridge east of the city and struck from their rear. The enemy fled; he pursued as far as Chuzhou before a blizzard forced him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 獲騾馬一千五百三十一、鞍六百，衣甲旗幟稱是。

translations.literal: They captured one thousand five hundred thirty-one mules and horses, six hundred saddles, clothing, armor, flags, and banners in comparable quantity.
translations.idiomatic: The haul included 1,531 mounts, 600 saddles, and a commensurate trove of armor, banners, and kit.

sentences.zh: 授忠州團練使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Tuanlian envoy of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regimental commissioner of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，除鎮江都統制兼權山東、京東招撫司事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was removed and appointed Jiangdu commander-in-chief, concurrently holding acting authority over Shandong and Jingdong Pacification Commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the reign he was named commander at Zhenjiang and given provisional charge of the Shandong and Jingdong pacification offices.

sentences.zh: 還至揚州，除驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Returning to Yangzhou, he was removed and appointed Xiaowei grand general.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Yangzhou he was promoted to Grand General of the Valiant Guards.

sentences.zh: 金圍楚州已三月，列屯六十餘里。

translations.literal: Jin had besieged Chuzhou already three months; they arrayed encampments for more than sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens had held Chuzhou under siege for three months, their camps strung out for sixty li.

sentences.zh: 再遇遣將分道撓擊，軍聲大振，楚圍解。

translations.literal: Zaiyu dispatched generals on separate routes to harass and strike; military renown greatly rose; the Chu siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zaiyu sent his officers to harry the enemy along several axes; the thunder of his advance broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 兼知揚州、淮東安撫使。

translations.literal: Concurrently he was made acting prefect of Yangzhou and Huaidong pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed prefect of Yangzhou and pacification commissioner for Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 揚州有北軍二千五百人，再遇請分隸建康、鎮江軍，每隊不過數人，使不得為變。

translations.literal: Yangzhou had Northern Army troops two thousand five hundred men; Zaiyu requested to divide and attach them subordinately to Jiankang and Zhenjiang armies; each squad had no more than several men, so they could not make a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou still housed 2,500 northern troops; Bi Zaiyu had them parceled out in tiny detachments to the Jiankang and Zhenjiang commands so they could not plot another mutiny.

sentences.zh: 更造輕甲，長不過膝，披不過肘，兜鍪亦殺重為輕，馬甲易以皮，車牌易以木而設轉軸其下，使一人之力可推可擎，務便捷不使重遲。

translations.literal: He remade light armor, length not exceeding the knee, cloak not exceeding the elbow; helmets also had weight cut to be light; horse armor was changed to leather; chariot shields changed to wood with pivot axles set beneath, so that one man's strength could push or lift them; he sought convenience and would not allow heaviness or delay.
translations.idiomatic: He redesigned the kit for mobility: cuirasses no longer than the knee, sleeves ending at the elbow, lighter helmets, leather horse bardings, and wooden shields mounted on pivots so a single soldier could carry or swing them—the whole apparatus built for speed, not ponderous protection.

sentences.zh: 敢死一軍，本烏合亡命，再遇能駕馭得其用。

translations.literal: A dare-to-die army, originally a motley crowd of desperate fugitives; Zaiyu could drive and control them and obtain their use.
translations.idiomatic: His Death-or-Glory regiment had begun as a rabble of outlaws, yet Bi Zaiyu bent them to disciplined service.

sentences.zh: 陳世雄、許俊等皆再遇所薦。

translations.literal: Chen Shixiong, Xu Jun, and others were all recommended by Zaiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Officers such as Chen Shixiong and Xu Jun rose through his patronage.

sentences.zh: 張健雄恃勇桀驁，再遇狀其罪於朝，命以軍法戮之，諸將懾服。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianxiong relied on bravery and was fierce and insubordinate; Zaiyu memorialized his crimes to the court; he was ordered executed by military law; all generals were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the swaggering Zhang Jianxiong defied command, Bi Zaiyu reported his offenses and had him executed under military law, cowing the rest of the officer corps into obedience.

sentences.zh: 再遇姿貌雄傑，早以拳力聞，屬時寢兵，無所自見。

translations.literal: Zaiyu's bearing and appearance were heroic and outstanding; early on he was renowned for boxing strength; as the times lay armies to rest, he had nowhere to show himself.
translations.idiomatic: A man of imposing physique famed since youth for his prowess in the ring, Bi Zaiyu had spent the long peace with no battlefield on which to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 一旦邊事起，諸將望風奔衄，再遇威聲始著，遂為名將云。

translations.literal: Once border affairs arose, numerous generals at sight of the wind fled in rout; Zaiyu's awesome renown first became manifest; he thus became a famous general, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When war flared on the frontier and other commanders melted away, his reputation finally took hold and he entered the ranks of the dynasty's great captains.

sentences.zh: 安丙，字子文，廣安人。

translations.literal: An Bing, style name Ziwen, a native of Guang'an.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing (zi Ziwen) was born in Guang'an.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間進士，調大足縣主簿。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Chunxi era; he was transferred to registrar of Dazu County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination during the Chunxi reign and received his first posting as registrar of Dazu County.

sentences.zh: 秩滿詣闕，陳蜀利病十五事，言皆剴切。

translations.literal: When his term ended he went to the imperial audience hall; he submitted fifteen items on Sichuan's benefits and harms; his words were all incisive and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he traveled to court and laid before the emperor fifteen pointed critiques of Sichuan's strengths and failures.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，辟利西安撫司幹辦公事，調曲水丞。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when mourning ended, he was recruited as handling affairs officer of the Lizhou Pacification Commission; he was transferred to Qu Shui assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his father, he joined the Lizhou pacification staff as an administrative officer and was later moved to assistant magistrate of Qushui.

sentences.zh: 吳挺為帥，知其才，邀致之。

translations.literal: Wu Ting served as commander; knowing his talent, he invited and brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Ting took command in Sichuan, he recognized An Bing's ability and brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 改秩，知新繁縣。

translations.literal: His rank was changed; he was made magistrate of Xinfan County.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in rank, he was appointed magistrate of Xinfan.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，知小溪縣。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when mourning ended, he was made magistrate of Xiaoxi County.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was assigned to govern Xiaoxi County.

sentences.zh: 通判隆慶府，嘉泰三年，郡大水，丙白守張鼎，發常平粟振之。

translations.literal: As tongpan of Longqing Prefecture, in the third year of Jiatai the commandery suffered great flood; Bing informed the prefect Zhang Ding and had regular-granary grain disbursed to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice-prefect of Longqing, he persuaded Prefect Zhang Ding to open the government granaries during the catastrophic floods of Jiatai year 3.

sentences.zh: 尋又鑿石徙溪，自是無水患。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he also carved stone and relocated the stream; from this time there were no flood calamities.
translations.idiomatic: He then redirected the riverbed through stone works that ended the seasonal inundations.

sentences.zh: 知大安軍，歲旱，民艱食，丙以家財即下流糴米數萬石以振。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Da'an Military Prefecture, in a drought year the people had difficulty obtaining food; Bing used family wealth to go downstream at once and purchase tens of thousands of piculs of rice to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Da'an, during a famine he spent his private fortune to buy tens of thousands of bushels of grain downstream and distribute it to the starving.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔加一秩。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict added one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of his charity and promoted him one grade.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，邊事方興，程松為四川宣撫使，吳曦副之，丙陳十可憂於松。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi, border affairs were just arising; Cheng Song was Sichuan Pacification Commissioner; Wu Xi was his deputy; Bing submitted ten worrisome points to Song.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Kaixi year 2, with Cheng Song as Sichuan commander and Wu Xi as his deputy, An Bing warned Song of ten impending dangers.

sentences.zh: 繼而松開府漢中，道三泉，夜延丙議。

translations.literal: Thereafter Song opened his headquarters at Hanzhong; on the road at Sanquan, at night he invited Bing to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Song later established his headquarters at Hanzhong and, pausing at Sanquan, summoned An Bing for a midnight council.

sentences.zh: 丙又為松言曦必誤國，松不省。

translations.literal: Bing again told Song that Xi would certainly harm the state; Song did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing again warned that Wu Xi would ruin the campaign, but Song dismissed the warning.

sentences.zh: 蓋丙嘗為其父客，素知曦。

translations.literal: The reason was that Bing had once been his father's client and from of old knew Xi.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing had served in the Wu household in his youth and knew Xi's character well.

sentences.zh: 既而曦奏丙為隨軍轉運司，居河池。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xi memorialized to make Bing attached-army transport commissioner; he resided at Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi soon had him appointed army transport commissioner and posted him at Hechi.

sentences.zh: 時梁、洋義士方襲取和尚原，旋為金人所奪，守將棄甲而走。

translations.literal: At the time Liang and Yang volunteer warriors had just raided and seized Heshang Plain; presently it was seized back by Jin people; the defending general cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Patriot militia from Liang and Yang prefectures had just retaken Heshang Plain, only to lose it again as the garrison commander fled without his armor.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊子，金人攻湫池堡，破天水，繇西和入成州，師潰，曦置不問。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi in the eleventh month, Jin people attacked Qiuchi Fort, broke through Tianshui, followed through Xihe into Chenzhou; the army collapsed; Xi set it aside and made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh month's wuzi day the Jurchens stormed Qiuchi Fort, overran Tianshui, and swept through Xihe into Chenzhou while the Song lines disintegrated. Wu Xi ignored the disaster.

sentences.zh: 金人肆掠關外四州，如踐虛邑，軍民莫知死所。

translations.literal: Jin people wantonly plundered the four prefectures beyond the pass; it was as if treading empty towns; soldiers and civilians knew not where to die.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens ravaged the four frontier prefectures as though marching through ghost towns; soldiers and civilians alike faced death with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 曦已潛遣其客姚淮源交金人，至是曦還興州，留丙魚關，已而檄還武興。

translations.literal: Xi had already secretly sent his client Yao Huaiyuan to interact with Jin people; by this time Xi returned to Xingzhou, leaving Bing at Yuguan; shortly he issued a dispatch summoning him back to Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi had already sent his agent Yao Huaiyuan to treat with the Jurchens. He returned to Xingzhou, leaving An Bing at Yuguan before recalling him to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，金人持其詔及金印至罝口，曦密受之，宣言使者欲得四州以和，馳書諷松去。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin in the twelfth month, Jin people brought their edict and gold seal to Zhakou; Xi secretly received them; he proclaimed the envoy wished to obtain the four prefectures for peace; he dispatched a letter hinting Song should leave.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth month's bingyin day Jin envoys arrived at Zhakou with an edict and golden seal; Wu Xi accepted them in secret and announced the enemy sought the four prefectures in exchange for peace, while urging Cheng Song to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，曦受金詔稱蜀王，榜諭四川。

translations.literal: On guiyou day, Xi received the Jin edict and styled himself King of Shu; he posted notices informing Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Wu Xi accepted the Jin investiture as King of Shu and issued proclamations across the province.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲午，曦僭號建官，稱臣於金，以其月為元年，改興州為興德府，以丙為中大夫、丞相長史、權行都省事。

translations.literal: On the third year, first month, jiawu day, Xi presumptuously established title and offices, styled himself subject of Jin, took that month as first year, changed Xingzhou to Xingde Prefecture, and made Bing Grand Master for Guidance, Chancellor Chief Steward, acting provisional Metropolitan Administration authority.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the first month of year 3, Wu Xi declared his own reign, submitted to the Jin as their vassal, renamed the calendar, transformed Xingzhou into Xingde Prefecture, and installed An Bing as Grand Master for Guidance, chief steward of the chancellery, and acting head of the metropolitan government.

sentences.zh: 先是，從事郎錢鞏之從曦在河池，嘗夢曦禱神祠，以銀杯為珓擲之，神起立謂曦曰：「公何疑？

translations.literal: Earlier, Associate Gentleman Qian Gongzhi followed Xi at Hechi; he once dreamed Xi prayed at a spirit shrine, taking a silver cup as casting lots and throwing them; the spirit stood up and said to Xi: "Lord, why doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving Wu Xi at Hechi, the clerk Qian Gongzhi dreamed that Xi prayed at a shrine, casting divination lots with a silver cup. The spirit rose and asked: "Why do you hesitate?

sentences.zh: 公何疑？

translations.literal: Lord, why doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Why hesitate? the spirit asked again.

sentences.zh: 後政事已分付安子文矣。」

translations.literal: Hereafter governance affairs have already been entrusted to An Ziwen.
translations.idiomatic: "Your affairs are already in the hands of An Ziwen," it said.

sentences.zh: 曦未省，神又曰：「安子文有才，足能辦此。」

translations.literal: 」Xi did not understand; the spirit again said: "An Ziwen has talent sufficient to handle this.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi did not grasp the omen until the spirit added: "An Ziwen has the talent to manage it all.

sentences.zh: 鞏之覺，心異其事，具以語曦。

translations.literal: 」When Gongzhi awoke, his heart found the matter strange; he fully related it to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian awoke disturbed by the vision and reported every detail to Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 事既熾，丙不得脫，度徒死無益，陽與而陰圖之。

translations.literal: The affair had already flared; Bing could not escape; he estimated that dying in vain would be without benefit; outwardly he assented while inwardly he plotted.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion fully underway, An Bing saw he could not escape without pointless martyrdom, so he feigned loyalty while plotting Xi's downfall.

sentences.zh: 遂與楊巨源、李好義等謀誅曦，語見《巨源》、《好義傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Yang Juyuan, Li Haoyi, and others he plotted to execute Xi; the account appears in the Juyuan and Haoyi biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yang Juyuan, Li Haoyi, and others to plan Wu Xi's assassination—the full story appears in their respective biographies.

sentences.zh: 徐景望在利州，逐土人，擅財賦。

translations.literal: Xu Jingwang was at Lizhou; he drove out the native people and monopolized finances and levies.
translations.idiomatic: At Lizhou, Xu Jingwang expelled local residents and seized control of tax revenues.

sentences.zh: 丙遣弟煥往約諸將，相與拊定，及景望伏誅，軍民無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: Bing dispatched his younger brother Huan to go and win over the generals; together they pacified and settled; when Jingwang was executed in secret, soldiers and civilians dared not clamor.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing sent his brother Huan to rally the commanders; once Xu Jingwang was executed, neither troops nor civilians dared stir.

sentences.zh: 於是傳檄諸道，按堵如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon they issued proclamations to all routes; peace and order remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamations went out to every circuit and the province returned to calm.

sentences.zh: 曦僭位凡四十一日。

translations.literal: Xi's presumptuous reign in all was forty-one days.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's usurpation lasted only forty-one days.

sentences.zh: 三月戊寅，陳曦所以反及矯制平賊便宜賞功狀，自劾待罪，函曦首級、違制法物與曦所受金人詔印及所匿庚牌附驛。

translations.literal: On the third month, day wuyin, he submitted the account of Xi's reasons for rebellion and, by forged edict, the authority to pacify bandits and reward merit as expedient; he impeached himself awaiting punishment; he enclosed Xi's severed head, illegal regulation objects, the Jin edict seal Xi received, and the concealed geng plaques; all were attached to the post relay.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's wuyin day he memorialized the full account of Wu Xi's treason, his emergency powers to suppress the revolt and reward the loyal, and a plea to accept punishment—sending by courier Xi's severed head, contraband regalia, the Jin seals, and the stolen tally plaques.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初聞變，莫知所為。

translations.literal: The court first heard of the uprising and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the rebellion first reached the capital, the court was paralyzed with uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄與曦書，亦謂「嗣頒茅土之封」，亟召知鎮江府宇文紹節問之，紹節曰：「安丙非附逆者，必能討賊。」

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou in correspondence with Xi also said "thereafter bestowing fief of commune and state"; he urgently summoned Acting Zhenjiang Prefect Yuwen Shao to question him; Shao said: "An Bing is not one who adheres to rebellion; he will certainly be able to suppress the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou's own letters to Wu Xi had hinted at enfeoffment, so the court urgently summoned Yuwen Shaojie, prefect of Zhenjiang, who declared: "An Bing is no traitor—he will bring down the rebel.

sentences.zh: 於是密降帛書曰：「安丙素推才具，有志事功，今聞曦謀不軌，爾為所脅，諒以凶焰方張，恐重為蜀禍，故權且從之爾，豈一日忘君父者？

translations.literal: 」Thereupon they secretly sent down a silk letter saying: "An Bing has long been praised for talent and capacity; he has the will to accomplish meritorious deeds; now hearing Xi's plot is improper, you were compelled by him; we understand the traitor's flame is just now spreading and you fear piling further calamity on Shu; therefore you temporized and followed him for the moment—how could you forget ruler and father for a single day?
translations.idiomatic: The court secretly drafted a silk edict: "We have long valued An Bing's ability and ambition. Knowing you were forced into Wu Xi's plot and feared worse ruin for Shu if you resisted outright, we understand you played along—surely you never forgot your sovereign and fatherland for a day.

sentences.zh: 如能圖曦報國，以明本心，即當不次推賞，雖二府之崇亦無所吝，更宜審度機便，務在成事，以副委屬之意。」

translations.literal: If you can plot Xi's downfall and repay the state, to clarify your original heart, then we will immediately grant exceptional rewards without stint—even the eminence of the two Grand Councils will not be withheld; you should further carefully gauge opportune moments, and your task must be to accomplish the affair, to fulfill the intent of our commission.
translations.idiomatic: Overthrow Xi and your true loyalty will be rewarded beyond measure, even to a Grand Councillor's seat—choose your moment wisely and bring the matter to success, as we entrust you to do.

sentences.zh: 帛書未至，露布已聞，上下動色交慶。

translations.literal: 」Before the silk letter arrived, the bulletin report was already heard; above and below changed countenance in mutual rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Before the secret edict even arrived, news of victory spread through the court and the realm erupted in celebration.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，加丙端明殿學士、中大夫、知興州、安撫使兼四川宣撫副使，詔獎諭，恩數視執政，如帛書旨也。

translations.literal: On xinchou day, Bing was added Duanming Hall academician, Grand Master for Guidance, magistrate of Xingzhou, pacification commissioner, concurrently Sichuan Pacification deputy commissioner; an edict commended and instructed him; his favor and count were treated as equal to the Chief Councillors; it matched the silk-letter intent.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day the court promoted him to Duanming academician, Grand Master for Guidance, prefect of Xingzhou, pacification commissioner, and deputy Sichuan commander, showering him with honors equal to a chief councillor—precisely as the secret edict had promised.

sentences.zh: 時都統孫忠銳由鳳州進攻大散關不克，統領強德等出奇道由松林堡破金砦，四月癸丑，克之。

translations.literal: At the time Overall Commander Sun Zhongrui advanced from Fengzhou to attack Dasanguan but did not overcome it; commander Qiang De and others on a strange route by way of Songlin Fort broke the Jin stockade; on the fourth month, day guichou, they overcame it.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Sun Zhongrui failed in a frontal assault on Dasanguan from Fengzhou until Qiang De's detour through Songlin Fort stormed the Jin fort on the fourth month's guichou day.

sentences.zh: 忠銳貪功吝財，賞罰迷繆，大失軍心，且速還鳳州，以關鑰付庸將陳顯。

translations.literal: Zhongrui was greedy for merit and stingy with wealth; rewards and punishments were confused and erroneous; he greatly lost the army's hearts; moreover he hastened to return to Fengzhou, entrusting the pass keys to the mediocre general Chen Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhongrui's greed and miserly discipline alienated his troops; he hurried back to Fengzhou and left the pass to the inept Chen Xian.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，大散關復陷。

translations.literal: On guiyou day, Dasanguan again fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Dasanguan fell again.

sentences.zh: 巨源自請收復，丙遣朱邦寧佐之。

translations.literal: Juyuan requested on his own to recover it; Bing dispatched Zhu Bangning to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Juyuan volunteered to retake the pass, and An Bing sent Zhu Bangning to support him.

sentences.zh: 丙深惡忠銳，檄赴司議事，欲廢之。

translations.literal: Bing deeply hated Zhongrui; he issued a dispatch summoning him to headquarters to discuss affairs, intending to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing despised Sun Zhongrui and summoned him to headquarters under pretense of consultation, planning his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 巨源至鳳，斬忠銳及其子揆，丙遂以忠銳附偽進表之罪聞於朝。

translations.literal: Juyuan reached Fengzhou; he beheaded Zhongrui and his son Kui; Bing thereupon reported to the court Zhongrui's crime of attaching to the false regime and submitting a memorial of advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Juyuan reached Fengzhou he executed Sun Zhongrui and his son Kui; An Bing then reported to court that Zhongrui had collaborated with the puppet regime.

sentences.zh: 先是，以誅曦功，巨源補朝奉郎，與通判差遣。

translations.literal: Earlier, for the merit of executing Xi, Juyuan was supplemented as Gentleman for Court Service, with concurrent vice-prefect assignment.
translations.idiomatic: For killing Wu Xi, Yang Juyuan had already been granted the rank of Court Gentleman with a vice-prefect appointment.

sentences.zh: 巨源遣其親校傅檜訴功於朝，語見《巨源傳》。

translations.literal: Juyuan dispatched his close officer Fu Huai to plead merit at the court; the account appears in the Juyuan biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Juyuan sent his aide Fu Huai to press his claims at court—as told in his biography.

sentences.zh: 於是丙拜疏丐閑。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bing submitted a memorial bowing to request retirement.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing then memorialized requesting leave from office.

sentences.zh: 至是，金人揭示境上，得丙首者與銀絹二萬匹兩，即授四川宣撫。

translations.literal: By this time, Jin people posted notice on the border: whoever obtained Bing's head would receive twenty thousand bolts of silk and taels of silver; he was immediately appointed Sichuan Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens posted a bounty of twenty thousand bolts of silk and taels of silver for his head—whereupon the Song appointed him Sichuan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時方議和，丙獨戒飭將士，恫疑虛喝，以攻為守，威聲甚著。

translations.literal: Peace was just then under discussion; Bing alone warned and disciplined soldiers and officers, using intimidation, doubt, empty bluster, taking attack as defense; his awesome renown was very manifest.
translations.idiomatic: While peace talks dragged on, An Bing alone kept his command sharp—bluffing, probing, and threatening attack as the best defense until his reputation terrified the enemy.

sentences.zh: 詔以蜀平，遣吳獵撫諭四川。

translations.literal: An edict, because Shu was pacified, dispatched Wu Lie to soothe and instruct Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: With Sichuan pacified, the court sent Wu Lie to reassure the province.

sentences.zh: 時沿邊關隘悉為金毀，丙遺時相書，謂：「西和一面，已修仇池，聚糧積芻，使軍民可守。

translations.literal: At the time along the border all passes were destroyed by Jin; Bing sent a letter to the chief minister saying: "On the Xihe front, Chichi Pool has already been repaired; grain and forage amassed; so that soldiers and civilians may hold it.
translations.idiomatic: With every border fort in ruins, An Bing wrote the chief minister: "On the Xihe line we have fortified Chichi Chi, stockpiled grain, and made the position tenable for troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 若敵至，則堅壁不戰，彼欲攻則不可，欲越則不敢。

translations.literal: If the enemy arrives, then hold walls firm and do not fight; they wish to attack but cannot; wish to pass over but dare not.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy comes, we hold behind strong walls without giving battle—they cannot take it by assault and dare not bypass it.

sentences.zh: 若西和可守，成州之境自不敢犯。

translations.literal: If Xihe can be held, Chenzhou's territory naturally they will not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Xihe and they will not dare breach Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 成州黑谷、南谷亦皆頓重兵。

translations.literal: Chenzhou's Heigu and Nangu also all station heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Heigu and Nangu in Chenzhou are likewise garrisoned with crack troops.

sentences.zh: 天水雖不可守，距天水十里所，見創白環堡，與西和相為掎角，又增堡雞頭山，咸以民卒守之，及修黃牛堡，築興趙原，屯千餘人。

translations.literal: Tianshui although cannot be held, ten li from Tianshui, we now create White Ring Fort, with Xihe as pincers from horn angles; again we add fort Jitou Mountain, all with civilian soldiers to guard them; and we repair Yellow Ox Fort, build Xingzhao Plain, station over a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui itself cannot be held, but ten li away we are building White Ring Fort to pincer with Xihe, strengthening Jitoushan, manning both with militia, repairing Huangniu Fort, and posting a thousand men at Xingzhao Plain.

sentences.zh: 鳳州秋防原尤為險絕，紹興初，州治於此，宣撫吳玠嘗作家計砦，前即馬嶺堡，正扼鳳州之後。

translations.literal: Fengzhou's Autumn Defense Plain is especially precipitous and absolute; in the beginning of the Shaoxing era, the prefecture government was located here; Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie once built Family-Planning stockade; in front lies Maling Fort, directly blocking Fengzhou's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou's Qiufang Plain is the most forbidding terrain—in early Shaoxing the prefectural seat stood here, where Wu Jie built his Jiaji stockade with Maling Fort ahead, commanding Fengzhou's rear.

sentences.zh: 凡此數堡既堅，金人決不敢近。

translations.literal: All these several forts being already firm, Jin people are resolved not to dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: With these bastions strengthened, the Jurchens will not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 而河池、殺金平、魚關皆大軍屯聚，其他徑路，雖關之裏如大安，亦陰招民卒，授以器械，為掩擊之備矣。」

translations.literal: Yet Hechi, Shajinping, and Yuguan all have great armies massed; other path routes, even passes within like Da'an, also covertly recruit civilian soldiers, grant them weapons, as preparation for ambush strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Hechi, Shajinping, and Yuguan concentrate our main forces; even inner routes such as Da'an secretly arm militia for ambush.

sentences.zh: 又云：「見於關表廣結義士，月給以糧，俾各保田廬墳墓，逮事定，則係之尺籍而勸之耕，庶可經久。

translations.literal: 」He also said: "As seen at the border passes, broadly enlist righteous warriors, monthly supply them grain, so that each may protect his fields, houses, and ancestral graves; when affairs settle, then attach them to the military register and encourage them to farm—so it may endure long.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed recruiting loyalists along the frontier, paying them monthly grain to guard their farms and ancestral graves until peace, then enrolling them for farming—a sustainable defense.

sentences.zh: 以丙所見，直為守計，則精選五萬人亦為有餘。」

translations.literal: By Bing's view, if purely for defense planning, then carefully selecting fifty thousand men is also more than enough."
translations.idiomatic: In my view," he concluded, "fifty thousand picked troops are ample for a defensive strategy alone."

sentences.zh: 好義守西和，謂四州兵後，民不聊生，請蠲租以惠創痍。

translations.literal: Haoyi guarded Xihe; he said the four prefectures' armies having been through warfare, the people had no leisure to live; he requested exemption from rent to benefit the wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi, governing Xihe, petitioned to remit taxes in the war-scarred four prefectures where the people could scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 丙請於朝。

translations.literal: Bing requested it of the court.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing forwarded the request to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又以沔州都統司所統十軍權太重，故自吳璘至挺、曦皆有尾大不掉之憂，乃請分置副都統制，各不相隸，以前右中左後五軍隸都統司，踏白、摧鋒、選鋒、策鋒、遊奕五軍隸副司。

translations.literal: Also because the Mianzhou Overall Command office's ten armies it commanded had authority too weighty, therefore from Wu Lin down to Ting and Xi all had the worry of the tail growing too large to wag; he thereupon requested dividing and establishing deputy overall commanders-in-chief, each not subordinate to the other; the former five armies Right, Center, Left, Rear subordinated to the Overall Command office; the Treading White, Crushing Vanguard, Selected Vanguard, Strategy Vanguard, and Roaming Patrol five armies subordinated to the deputy office.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that the ten armies under the Mianzhou command had grown too powerful—every commander from Wu Lin to Wu Ting and Wu Xi had faced the same fear of armies too strong to control. He proposed splitting them between a commander and a deputy, with the Right, Center, Left, Front, and Rear armies under the main command and the Treading White, Crushing Vanguard, Selected Vanguard, Strategy Vanguard, and Roaming Patrol armies under the deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: Edicts all followed his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時方信孺使還，金人和意未決，且欲得首議興師之人，侂胄大怒。

translations.literal: At the time Fang Xinru's mission returned; Jin harmony will was not settled; they moreover wished to obtain the person who first proposed launching the army; Tuozhou was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru returned from the Jin court with peace still uncertain and a demand for whoever had started the war—enraging Han Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 上手書賜丙，謂：「金人必再至，當激勵將士，戮力赴功。」

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote and bestowed on Bing, saying: "Jin people will certainly come again; you should exhort and urge soldiers and officers, joining strength to rush to merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote personally to An Bing: "The Jurchens will return—stir your commanders to zeal and shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 侂胄既誅，賜丙金器百二十兩、細幣二十匹，進資政殿學士。

translations.literal: 」After Tuozhou was executed, Bing was granted one hundred twenty liang of gold vessels and twenty bolts of fine silks; he was advanced to Zizheng Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou's execution the court rewarded An Bing with 120 taels of gold vessels and twenty bolts of fine silk, promoting him to Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還大散、隔牙關。

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was concluded, Dasanguan and Geya Pass were returned.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty restored Dasanguan and Geya Pass.

sentences.zh: 丙分遣僚吏，經量洋、沔、興元、大安民田，別定租稅。

translations.literal: Bing separately dispatched subordinate officials to survey and measure civilian fields in Yang, Mian, Xingyuan, and Da'an; separately fixing rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing dispatched officers to survey farmland in Yang, Mian, Xingyuan, and Da'an and set new tax rates.

sentences.zh: 右丞相史彌遠起復，丙移書曰：「昔仁宗起復富鄭公、文潞公，孝宗起復蔣丞相，皆力辭，名教所係，人言可畏，望閣下速辭成命，以息議者之口。」

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Shi Miyuan was recalled from mourning; Bing sent a letter saying: "In the past Emperor Renzong recalled from mourning Fu the Duke of Zheng and Wen the Duke of Lu; Emperor Xiaozong recalled Chancellor Jiang—all strenuously declined. Name-and-principle teaching is what is bound; people's words are to be feared. I hope Your Excellency will quickly decline to complete the mandate, to quiet the mouths of critics.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan left mourning to resume office, An Bing wrote urging him to refuse as esteemed statesmen from Fu Kuan and Wen Yanbo to Jiang Gong had done—ritual and public opinion demanded it, and he should decline quickly to silence critics.

sentences.zh: 論者韙之。

translations.literal: 」Commentators praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators applauded the letter.

sentences.zh: 升大學士、四川制置大使兼知興元府。

translations.literal: He was raised to Grand Academician, Sichuan Military Preparation Grand Ambassador, concurrently magistrate of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Grand Academician, Sichuan military commissioner, and prefect of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 諜知金人遷汴，關輔豪傑款塞願降者眾。

translations.literal: Through spies it was learned that the Jin people had moved to Bian; Guanfu heroes knocking at the passes wishing to surrender were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that the Jurchens had relocated to Kaifeng, and many frontier stalwarts along the passes were offering to defect.

sentences.zh: 丙以為此正冉閔告晉之時，乃與宰臣書，謂當興問罪之師。

translations.literal: Bing thought this was exactly the time when Ran Min reported to Jin; he then wrote to the chief ministers, saying they ought to raise an army to demand justice.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing saw the moment as parallel to Ran Min's appeal to Jin for aid against barbarians, and urged the councillors to launch a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 朝論憂丙輕舉，乃詔丙益修守備。

translations.literal: Court discussion worried Bing acted lightly; an edict ordered Bing further to repair guard preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Critics at court feared he was too rash, and the throne ordered him instead to strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 七年春，丙使所愛吏安蕃、何九齡合官軍夜襲秦州，敗歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year spring, Bing sent his beloved clerks An Fan and He Jiuling to combine with government troops and night-raid Qinzhou; they were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he sent his favorites An Fan and He Jiuling with regular troops on a night assault against Qinzhou; they were routed and driven back.

sentences.zh: 王大才執九齡等七人斬之，而訟丙於朝。

translations.literal: Wang Dacai arrested Jiuling and six other men and beheaded them, and thereupon impeached Bing at court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dacai seized Jiuling and six others, executed them, and memorialized against An Bing at the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔丙同知樞密院事兼太子賓客，賜手書召之。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict appointed Bing Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrent Crown Prince Preceptor, bestowing a personal letter summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court named him vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and crown prince preceptor, summoning him with an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 行次廣德軍，進觀文殿學士、知潭州、湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: En route he stopped at Guangde Army; he was advanced to Guanwen Hall academician, magistrate of Tanzhou, and Hunan Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling he was promoted at Guangde to Guanwen Hall academician, prefect of Tanzhou, and pacification commissioner for Hunan.

sentences.zh: 至官，留意學校，請於太常創大成樂。

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he paid attention to schools and requested of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to create the Great Completion music.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he devoted himself to education and petitioned the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to establish the Dacheng ritual music.

sentences.zh: 而政尚嚴酷，轉運判官章徠劾丙，不報。

translations.literal: Yet his government still leaned toward severity; Transport Circuit judge Zhang Lai impeached Bing, and there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His rule remained harsh; transport judge Zhang Lai impeached him, but the court took no action.

sentences.zh: 御史李安行並徠劾之，徠罷，丙授崇信軍節度使、開府儀同三司、萬壽觀使。

translations.literal: Censor Li Anxing together with Lai impeached him; Lai was dismissed, and Bing was appointed Chongxin Army military commissioner, Grand Master of Splendid Honors with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and superintendent of Wanshou Abbey.
