translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Anxing joined Zhang Lai in the attack; Zhang was removed, while An Bing was made military commissioner of Chongxin, granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and named superintendent of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 譴閣門舍人聞人璵錫命，賜旌節、金印、衣帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He dispatched a Gatehouse Attendant, Wenren Yu, to convey the mandate, bestowing banners and credentials, a gold seal, belt and sash, saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant, Wenren Yu, was sent with the commission, bearing insignia of office, a gold seal, robes, belt, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 三辭，還蜀。

translations.literal: He declined three times and returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After thrice declining the honors he went back to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 董居誼帥蜀，大失士心。

translations.literal: Dong Juyi commanded Shu and greatly lost the hearts of officers.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Juyi as commander of Sichuan had alienated the officer corps.

sentences.zh: 金人乘之，破赤丹、黃牛堡，入武休關，直搗梁、洋，至大安，宋師所至輒潰，散入巴山。

translations.literal: Jin people seized the opportunity, broke Chidan and Huangniu forts, entered Wuxiu Pass, drove straight against Liang and Yang, reaching Da'an; wherever Song armies went they at once collapsed, scattering into Ba Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pressed the advantage, storming Chidan and Huangniu forts, breaking through Wuxiu Pass, and thrusting toward Liang and Yang as far as Da'an; Song forces melted away wherever they met the enemy and fled into the Ba hills.

sentences.zh: 十二年，聶子述代之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Nie Zishu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Nie Zishu replaced him as commander.

sentences.zh: 時丙之子癸仲知果州，子述即檄兼參議官。

translations.literal: At the time Bing's son Guizhong was magistrate of Guozhou; Zishu at once issued a dispatch appointing him concurrent deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing's son Guizhong was then prefect of Guozhou, and Zishu immediately named him joint staff adviser by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 四月，紅巾賊張福、莫簡叛，入利州，子述遁去。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Red Turban bandits Zhang Fu and Mo Jian rebelled, entered Lizhou, and Zishu fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Red Turban rebels Zhang Fu and Mo Jian rose, seized Lizhou, and Zishu fled.

sentences.zh: 總領財賦楊九鼎與賊遇，走匿民舍，賊追九鼎殺之。

translations.literal: Overall fiscal intendant Yang Jiuding encountered the bandits, ran and hid in a civilian house; the bandits pursued and killed Jiuding.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal intendant Yang Jiuding met the rebels, hid in a farmhouse, and was hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 子述退保劍門，檄癸仲兼節制軍馬，任討賊之責。

translations.literal: Zishu withdrew to guard Jianmen, dispatched Guizhong as concurrent controller of army and horse, charging him with the duty of suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zishu fell back to Jianmen Pass and ordered Guizhong to take command of the troops and bear responsibility for crushing the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 癸仲召戎帥張威等軍來會，賊自閬趨遂寧，所過無不殘滅。

translations.literal: Guizhong summoned frontier commanders Zhang Wei and others' armies to assemble; the bandits from Lang advanced toward Suining, and wherever they passed nothing escaped devastation.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhong gathered frontier generals including Zhang Wei; the rebels marched from Langzhou toward Suining, leaving ruin in every place they touched.

sentences.zh: 丙欲自持十萬緡偕子述往益昌募士，子述曰：「大臣非得上旨，未可輕出。」

translations.literal: Bing wished to take one hundred thousand strings of cash himself and go with Zishu to Yichang to recruit warriors; Zishu said: "A great minister, without obtaining the ruler's directive, must not lightly go out."
translations.idiomatic: An Bing wanted to carry a hundred thousand strings of cash to Yichang with Zishu to raise troops, but Zishu warned, "A senior minister may not leave his post without explicit imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 丙遂如果州。

translations.literal: Bing thereupon went to Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing then proceeded to Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 時四川大震，甚於曦之變。

translations.literal: At the time Sichuan was greatly shaken, more severe than Xi's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was in turmoil worse than Wu Xi's revolt.

sentences.zh: 張方首奏，勳望如丙，今猶可用。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang memorialized first, saying merit and prestige like Bing's could still be employed now.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang memorialized first that a man of An Bing's stature and renown could still be put to use.

sentences.zh: 魏了翁移書宰執，謂安丙不起，則賊未即平，蜀未可定，雖賊亦曰：「須安相公作宣撫，事乃定耳。」

translations.literal: Wei Liaoweng sent a letter to the chief ministers, saying if An Bing did not rise, then the bandits would not at once be pacified and Shu could not be settled; even the bandits also said: "We must have Chancellor An made Pacification Commissioner—only then will affairs be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liaoweng wrote the chief ministers that without An Bing the rebels would not soon be crushed nor Sichuan secured—even the rebels were saying, "Only when Chancellor An becomes pacification commissioner will things be settled."

sentences.zh: 李壁、李篁時並鎮潼、遂，亦皆以國事勉丙。

translations.literal: Li Bi and Li Huang at the time both commanded Tong and Sui, and they too all used state affairs to urge Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and Li Huang, then commanding Tongzhou and Suining, likewise pressed him in the name of the realm.

sentences.zh: 五月乙未，丙至果州，是日賊焚蓬溪縣。

translations.literal: On the yiyi day of the fifth month, Bing reached Guozhou; that same day the bandits burned Pengxi County.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyi day of the fifth month An Bing reached Guozhou; that same day the rebels burned Pengxi County.

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔起丙為四川宣撫使，予便宜，尋降制授保寧軍節度使兼知興元府、利東安撫使。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day, an edict recalled Bing as Sichuan Pacification Commissioner, granting discretionary authority; soon an imperial rescript appointed him Baoning Army military commissioner, concurrently magistrate of Xingyuan Prefecture and Eastern Li Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day the court recalled him as Sichuan pacification commissioner with full discretionary powers, then formally named him military commissioner of Baoning, prefect of Xingyuan, and pacification commissioner for eastern Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 丙奏：「臣不辭老以報國，但事不任怨，難以圖成，將恐騰謗交攻，使臣獨抱赤心，無從上白。

translations.literal: Bing memorialized: "Your servant does not decline old age in repaying the state, but affairs that do not bear resentment are hard to bring to completion; I fear slander will surge and attack together, leaving your servant alone clutching a loyal heart with no means to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing submitted: "I do not shirk age in serving the dynasty, yet work that invites no blame is hard to finish; I fear a storm of slander will leave my loyalty unheard at court.

sentences.zh: 昔秦使甘茂攻宜陽，至質之以『息壤在彼』，魏使樂羊攻中山，至示之以謗書一篋。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin sent Gan Mao to attack Yiyang, until they pledged to him with 'the covenant earth is there'; Wei sent Yue Yang to attack Zhongshan, until they showed him a basket of slander letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin sent Gan Mao against Yiyang, the king pledged with him the covenant at Xitu; when Wei sent Yue Yang against Zhongshan, the ruler opened a chest of denunciations to prove his trust.

sentences.zh: 君臣之間，似不必爾。

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister, it seems there need not be such things.
translations.idiomatic: Between sovereign and minister such measures ought not be necessary.

sentences.zh: 然自古及今，謗以疑間而成，禍以忌嫉而得；

translations.literal: Yet from antiquity to the present, slander is completed through suspicion and estrangement, and calamity is obtained through envy and jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: Yet from antiquity to the present slander grows from suspicion and estrangement, and ruin comes of envy and jealousy;

sentences.zh: 況臣已傷弓於既往，豈容不懲沸於方來。」

translations.literal: how much more when your servant has already been wounded by the bow in what is past—how could one not take warning from boiling water yet to come?"
translations.idiomatic: and I have already been wounded once by the bow—how could I ignore the kettle already boiling ahead?"

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔唐太宗以西寇未平，詔起李靖，靖慷慨請行，不以老疾為解。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang, because western bandits were not yet pacified, issued an edict recalling Li Jing; Jing fervently requested to go, not using old age and illness as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When Taizong faced unrest in the west he recalled Li Jing, who volunteered eagerly and refused to plead age or infirmity.

sentences.zh: 代宗有朔方之難，圖任郭子儀，聞命引道，亦不以讒惎自疑。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong had the Shuo-fang crisis and planned to employ Guo Ziyi; on hearing the command he led the way, likewise not using slander and suspicion to doubt himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong faced crisis in Shuofang he entrusted Guo Ziyi, who marched at once and would not let calumny shake his resolve.

sentences.zh: 皆能乘時立功，焜燿竹帛，朕甚慕之。

translations.literal: All were able to seize the time and establish merit, blazing glory on bamboo and silk; We greatly admire them.
translations.idiomatic: Both seized their moment and left their names shining in the histories—I hold them in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 今蜀道俶擾，未寬顧憂，朕起卿燕閑，付以方面，而卿忠於報國，誼不辭難，朕之用人庶幾於唐宗，卿之事朕無愧於李、郭矣。

translations.literal: Now the Shu roads are in sudden turmoil and care is not yet eased; We have raised you from leisure to entrust a frontier region, while you are loyal in repaying the state and in righteousness do not decline difficulty—Our employment of men is nearly like the Tang emperors', and your service to Us is without shame before Li and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Shu routes are in turmoil and my mind is not at ease; I have called you from retirement to a frontier command, and your loyalty in accepting hardship matches Tang Taizong's choice of men—your service to me need not fear comparison with Li Jing and Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 勉圖雋功，以濟國事！」

translations.literal: Strive to plan lofty merit to rescue state affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Strive for a splendid victory to settle the realm's troubles!

sentences.zh: 尋命丁焴改知興元府。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered Ding Huang transferred to be magistrate of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reassigned Ding Huang to govern Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲申，發果州。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day, he set out from Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day he marched out from Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，至遂寧，賊猶負固於普州之茗山。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day, he reached Suining; the bandits still stubbornly held out at Puzhou's Mingshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day he reached Suining while the rebels still held Mingshan in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙下令諸軍合圍，絕其樵汲之路以困之。

translations.literal: Bing ordered all armies to join in encirclement, cutting off their firewood-gathering and water-drawing routes to weary them.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing ordered a combined encirclement, cutting off firewood and water to starve them out.

sentences.zh: 未幾，張威、李貴俘獲張福等十七人以獻，丙命臠王大才以祭九鼎。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhang Wei and Li Gui captured Zhang Fu and seventeen others and presented them; Bing ordered Wang Dacai dismembered to sacrifice to Jiuding.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Wei and Li Gui captured Zhang Fu and seventeen others; An Bing had Wang Dacai dismembered as an offering to avenge Yang Jiuding.

sentences.zh: 七月庚子，盡俘餘黨千餘人，皆斬之。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the seventh month, all remaining partisans over a thousand men were captured and all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the seventh month more than a thousand remaining rebels were taken and executed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌班師，乃移治利州，賜保寧軍節度使印。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day the army returned in triumph; he then moved his administration to Lizhou and was granted the Baoning Army military commissioner's seal.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day he withdrew in triumph, moved his headquarters to Lizhou, and received the seal of the Baoning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 癸仲亦加三秩，進直華文閣，起復，主管宣撫司機宜文字。

translations.literal: Guizhong also received three ranks of promotion, advanced to direct attendance at the Zhiwen Pavilion, recalled from mourning, and supervised Pacification Commission staff planning documents.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhong was promoted three ranks, made a direct attendant of the Zhiwen Pavilion, recalled from mourning, and placed in charge of the pacification commission staff.

sentences.zh: 明年，進丙少保，賜衣帶鞍馬。

translations.literal: The next year, Bing was advanced to Junior Guardian and granted robes, belt, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: The following year An Bing was made Junior Guardian and given robes, belt, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 丙以關表營田多遺利，命官括之。

translations.literal: Bing, because border-pass garrison farms had much uncollected profit, ordered officials to inventory them.
translations.idiomatic: Finding much uncollected revenue on frontier garrison farms, An Bing ordered officials to audit them.

sentences.zh: 有文垓者，方持母喪，以便宜起復，幹辦魚關糧料院，俾之措置，且以宣撫副使印假之。

translations.literal: There was one Wen Gai, who was observing mourning for his mother; by discretionary authority he was recalled from mourning to manage the Yuguan grain supply office, was made to arrange matters, and the Pacification Deputy's seal was lent to him.
translations.idiomatic: One Wen Gai was still in mourning for his mother when Bing recalled him by emergency authority to run the Yuguan grain office, entrusted him with the audits, and lent him the deputy pacification commissioner's seal.

sentences.zh: 而馮安世者，又即利州置根括局。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Feng Anshi again at Lizhou established a root-inventory bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Anshi meanwhile set up another audit bureau at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是了翁遺丙書，謂：「幕府舉辟，當用經術信厚之士，不可用冒喪之人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liaoweng sent Bing a letter, saying: "Staff recruitment in the headquarters should employ men of classical learning, trustworthiness, and depth; one must not employ men who violate mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liaoweng then wrote An Bing: "Your staff should be men of learning and integrity, not men who break mourning law.

sentences.zh: 且公八年鎮蜀，有恩則有怨，豈可人人而校，事事而理，自處甚狹，恐貽子孫賓客無窮之累。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Excellency for eight years has garrisoned Shu—where there is favor there is also resentment; how can one settle accounts with every man and reason out every affair? You place yourself very narrowly and I fear you will bequeath endless burdens to your sons, grandsons, and retainers.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years governing Sichuan you have made friends and enemies alike—if you settle every score and pursue every grievance you narrow your path and may burden your heirs and clients without end.

sentences.zh: 雖今日理財難拘故常，然告絕產、首白契、訐隱田、伺富民過失、糾鹽酒戶虧額，報怨挾憤、招權納賄者，必且紛然，而公任其怨。」

translations.literal: Although today managing finances is hard to bind by old constants, yet those who report extinct estates, denounce blank contracts, expose hidden fields, watch wealthy households' faults, impeach salt and wine households' shortfalls—men who repay grudges, harbor anger, seek power, and accept bribes—will surely swarm, while Your Excellency bears their resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Even if revenue work cannot follow old rules, informers denouncing abandoned estates, blank deeds, hidden fields, wealthy men's faults, and salt and wine shortfalls—men nursing grudges, trading power for bribes—will multiply, and you will bear every hatred."

sentences.zh: 丙復書曰：「關外糴買當用四百萬緡，而總所見緡止二十五萬，多方措置，非得已而不已。

translations.literal: Bing replied in a letter: "Grain purchases beyond the passes ought to use four million strings of cash, yet the overall office's visible strings stop at two hundred fifty thousand; arranging by many paths, one cannot stop until there is no choice but to stop.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing answered: "Frontier grain purchases require four million strings of cash, yet the treasury shows only two hundred fifty thousand—we must improvise until there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 儻皆清流，何由辦事？

translations.literal: If all were pure-stream men, by what means could affairs be handled?
translations.idiomatic: If I used only spotless scholars, how would anything get done?

sentences.zh: 蜀士中如令弟嘉父、李成之輩，清則清、高則高矣，其肯辦錢穀俗務乎？

translations.literal: Among Shu scholars such as your younger brother Jiafu and Li Chengzhi and the like—pure if pure, lofty if lofty—would they be willing to handle money, grain, and vulgar tasks?
translations.idiomatic: Men like your brother Jiafu and Li Chengzhi are pure and lofty—would they touch grain accounts and vulgar business?

sentences.zh: 劉德修嘗雅責楊嗣勳不能舉義誅叛，嗣勳云：『德修特未當局耳。』

translations.literal: Liu Dexiu once elegantly reproached Yang Sixun for not raising righteousness to execute rebels; Sixun said: 'Dexiu simply has not yet held office.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dexiu once rebuked Yang Sixun for failing to rise against traitors; Sixun replied, "Dexiu has simply never held real office."

sentences.zh: 丙於華父亦云。」

translations.literal: Bing said the same to Huafu."
translations.idiomatic: An Bing said the same to Wei Liaoweng."

sentences.zh: 其後，安世不法滋甚，近臣有以書抵丙，而安世之徒亦發其事，丙械送大安窮治之。

translations.literal: Later, Anshi's unlawful conduct grew ever worse; a court intimate sent a letter reaching Bing, while Anshi's faction also exposed the affair; Bing sent him in fetters to Da'an for exhaustive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Feng Anshi's abuses worsened; a court intimate wrote An Bing, and Anshi's faction exposed the matter; An Bing sent him in chains to Da'an for a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 先是，夏人來乞師並兵攻金人，丙且奏且行，分遣將士趨秦、鞏、鳳翔，委丁焴節制，師次於鞏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xia people came requesting troops to join forces attacking Jin people; Bing both memorialized and marched, separately dispatching generals and soldiers toward Qin, Gong, and Fengxiang, entrusting control to Ding Huang; the army halted at Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tanguts had asked for Song troops to join them against the Jurchens; An Bing memorialized and marched at once, sending columns toward Qin, Gong, and Fengxiang under Ding Huang's command, halting at Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人以樞密使甯子寧眾二十餘萬，約以夏兵野戰，宋師攻城。

translations.literal: The Xia people had Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Ning Zining with a host of more than two hundred thousand; they agreed that Xia troops would fight in the field while Song armies besieged cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts fielded more than two hundred thousand men under Commissioner Ning Zining, agreeing that Tangut forces would fight in the open while Song troops stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 既而攻鞏不克，乃已。

translations.literal: Afterward the attack on Gong did not succeed, and they then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The assault on Gong failed, and the campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 丙卒，訃聞，以少傅致仕，輟視朝二日，贈少師，賻銀絹千計，賜沔州祠額為「英惠廟」。

translations.literal: Bing died; when the death report arrived, he was given Junior Mentor emeritus status; court audiences were suspended two days; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor; condolence silver and silks numbered in the thousands; Mianzhou temple plaque was granted as "Temple of Heroic Favor."
translations.idiomatic: An Bing died; on the news of his death he was recorded as Junior Mentor emeritus, court audiences were suspended for two days, he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor, granted thousands in silver and silk, and a temple at Mianzhou was named the Temple of Heroic Favor.

sentences.zh: 理宗親劄賜諡「忠定」。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong personally wrote a note bestowing the posthumous title "Loyal and Settled."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong personally wrote to grant the posthumous name Zhongding, "Loyal and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 丙所著有《皛然集》。

translations.literal: Works composed by Bing include the Collected Writings of Bright Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing's writings included the Collected Writings of Bright Clarity.

sentences.zh: 楊巨源

translations.literal: Yang Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Yang Juyuan.

sentences.zh: 楊巨源，字子淵，其先成都人。

translations.literal: Yang Juyuan, style name Ziyuan, his ancestors were men of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Juyuan, courtesy name Ziyuan, was descended from a Chengdu family.

sentences.zh: 父信臣，客益昌，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Xinchen was a guest at Yichang and thereupon made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinchen had settled at Yichang as a sojourner, and the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 巨源倜儻有大志，善騎射，涉獵諸子百家之書。

translations.literal: Juyuan was free-spirited and had great ambition, skilled at riding and archery, ranging through the books of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan was bold and ambitious, an expert horseman and archer who had read widely in the classics and philosophers.

sentences.zh: 應進士不中，武舉又不中。

translations.literal: He responded to the jinshi examination and did not pass; the military examination also he did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the civil service examination and the military examination alike.

sentences.zh: 劉光祖見而異之，薦之總領錢糧陳曄，以右職舉為鳳州堡子原倉官，馳騁射獵，傾財養士，沿邊忠義，咸服其才。

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, recommended him to overall grain intendant Chen Ye; by right-office nomination he was made Fengzhou Baoziyuan granary officer; he galloped in hunting and archery, poured out wealth to nurture warriors, and along the border the righteous and loyal all submitted to his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu was struck by him and recommended him to fiscal intendant Chen Ye, who appointed him granary officer at Fengzhou's Baoziyuan; he rode and hunted tirelessly, spent his fortune keeping men, and won the respect of loyalists along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 分差魚關糧料院，移監興州合江贍軍倉。

translations.literal: He was assigned to the Yuguan grain supply office, then transferred to supervise Xingzhou's Hejiang army provision granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Yuguan grain office and later put in charge of the Hejiang provision granary at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，巨源陰有討賊志，結義士三百人，給其錢糧。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, Juyuan secretly had the will to suppress the bandit, joining three hundred righteous warriors and supplying them money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, Juyuan secretly resolved to destroy him, gathering three hundred loyalists and paying their keep.

sentences.zh: 有遊奕軍統領張林者，力能挽兩石弓，隊將朱邦寧身長六尺，勇力過人，皆為曦所忌，雖屢戰有功亦不加賞，林等憾之。

translations.literal: There was a Roaming Patrol Army commander Zhang Lin, whose strength could draw a two-stone bow; company leader Zhu Bangning was six feet tall with courage and strength surpassing others; all were envied by Xi, and though they repeatedly fought with merit they received no added reward—Lin and the others resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming Patrol commander Zhang Lin could draw a two-stone bow; company leader Zhu Bangning stood six feet tall with exceptional strength; Xi envied them both and though they fought well gave them no reward, leaving them bitter.

sentences.zh: 時林在罝口，邦寧在合江，巨源因與深相締結，並集忠義人朱福、陳安、傅檜之徒。

translations.literal: At the time Lin was at Zhekou and Bangning at Hejiang; Juyuan therefore formed deep bonds with them, and together gathered righteous men Zhu Fu, Chen An, Fu Gui, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was then at Zhekou and Bangning at Hejiang; Juyuan bound himself closely to them and rallied loyalists including Zhu Fu, Chen An, and Fu Gui.

sentences.zh: 曦脅安丙為丞相長史，丙稱疾，眉士程夢錫見丙，丙歎曰：「世事如此，世無豪傑！」

translations.literal: Xi coerced An Bing to be chief minister chief steward; Bing claimed illness; Meizhou scholar Cheng Mengxi visited Bing, and Bing sighed: "Affairs of the age are thus—there are no heroes in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi forced An Bing to serve as his chief minister's chief steward; Bing feigned illness; when Meizhou scholar Cheng Mengxi visited him, An Bing sighed, "The times are desperate and there is not a hero among us!"

sentences.zh: 夢錫因及巨源之謀。

translations.literal: Mengxi thereupon mentioned Juyuan's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxi then spoke of Juyuan's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 丙曰：「肯見我乎？」

translations.literal: Bing said: "Is he willing to see me?"
translations.idiomatic: An Bing asked, "Will he come to me?"

sentences.zh: 乃囑夢錫以書致巨源，延之臥所。

translations.literal: He then instructed Mengxi to send a letter summoning Juyuan and received him in his sickroom.
translations.idiomatic: He had Mengxi write to summon Juyuan and received him at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 巨源曰：「先生而為逆賊丞相長史耶？」

translations.literal: Juyuan said: "Sir, and yet you serve as the rebel traitor's chief minister chief steward?"
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "You serve as chief steward to a rebel traitor?"

sentences.zh: 丙號哭曰：「目前兵將，我所知，不能奮起。

translations.literal: Bing wailed aloud: "The soldiers and generals before me, whom I know, cannot rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing wept aloud: "The commanders I know will not stir themselves.

sentences.zh: 必得豪傑，乃滅此賊，則丙無復憂。」

translations.literal: One must obtain a hero—only then can this bandit be destroyed, and then Bing will have no further worry."
translations.idiomatic: Only a hero can destroy this traitor, and then I shall have no more cares."

sentences.zh: 巨源曰：「先生之意決乎？」

translations.literal: Juyuan said: "Is Sir's intent settled?"
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan asked, "Is your resolve firm?"

sentences.zh: 丙指天誓曰：「若誅此賊，雖死為忠鬼，夫復何恨！」

translations.literal: Bing pointed to Heaven and swore: "If this bandit is executed, though I die I shall be a loyal ghost—what regret would remain!"
translations.idiomatic: An Bing pointed to Heaven and swore, "If we kill this traitor, I shall die a loyal ghost without regret!"

sentences.zh: 巨源大喜，曰：「非先生不足以主此事，非巨源不足以了此事。」

translations.literal: Juyuan was greatly pleased and said: "Without Sir there is not enough to preside over this affair; without Juyuan there is not enough to complete this affair."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan rejoiced and said, "Without you this plot cannot be led; without me it cannot be finished."

sentences.zh: 當是時，李好義、好問亦結李貴、楊君玉、李坤辰凡數十人，坤辰邀巨源與好義會。

translations.literal: At that time Li Haoyi and Haowen also joined Li Gui, Yang Junyu, Li Kunchen, and several tens of men; Kunchen invited Juyuan and Haoyi to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Haoyi and his brother Haowen had gathered Li Gui, Yang Junyu, Li Kunchen, and dozens of others; Kunchen brought Juyuan and Haoyi together.

sentences.zh: 巨源又大喜曰：「吾與安長史議以三月六日邀曦謁廟，合勇士刺之。」

translations.literal: Juyuan again rejoiced greatly and said: "I with Chief Steward An have planned on the sixth day of the third month to invite Xi to attend the temple, gathering brave warriors to stab him."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan exulted again: "Chief Steward An and I have planned to lure Xi to the temple on the sixth of the third month and strike him down with our brave men."

sentences.zh: 好義曰：「彼出則齪巷，從衛且千人，事必難濟。

translations.literal: Haoyi said: "When he goes out the lanes are narrow, his escort nearly a thousand men—the affair will surely be hard to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi objected: "When he goes abroad the alleys are cramped and his guard numbers a thousand—the plan cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 聞熟食日祭東園，圖之此其時也。」

translations.literal: I hear that on the Cold Food Festival day he sacrifices at the Eastern Garden—plotting it then is the time."
translations.idiomatic: I hear he will sacrifice at the Eastern Garden on Cold Food Day—that is our moment."

sentences.zh: 巨源然之。

translations.literal: Juyuan approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 好義願一見長史以為信。

translations.literal: Haoyi wished once to see the Chief Steward as proof of trust.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi asked to meet the chief steward himself as proof of good faith.

sentences.zh: 巨源曰：「吾今先為長史言之，來日偽宮，令長史問君先世是已。」

translations.literal: Juyuan said: "I will now first speak to the Chief Steward for you; tomorrow at the false palace, I shall have the Chief Steward ask whether your forebears were such-and-such—that will be the sign."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "I shall speak to him first; tomorrow at the rebel palace he will ask about your ancestors—that will be the signal."

sentences.zh: 巨源以告丙，明日，好義在偽宮見丙，揖之。

translations.literal: Juyuan told Bing; the next day Haoyi saw Bing at the false palace and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan informed An Bing; the next day Haoyi met him at the rebel palace and bowed.

sentences.zh: 丙曰：「鄉與尊父同僚，楊省幹盛談才略，旦夕以職事相委。」

translations.literal: Bing said: "In the countryside I was colleague with your honored father; Staff Officer Yang greatly praised your talent and strategy—I shall soon entrust you with official duties."
translations.idiomatic: An Bing said, "Your father and I served together in the provinces; Staff Officer Yang has praised your talents highly, and I shall soon place duties in your hands."

sentences.zh: 其謀乃決。

translations.literal: Their plot was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The conspiracy was sealed.

sentences.zh: 君玉先屬其鄉人白子申擬詔，文不雅馴，巨源更為之，例用合江倉朱記。

translations.literal: Junyu first had his fellow townsman Bai Zishen draft the edict; the text was not elegant and tame; Juyuan rewrote it, following precedent by using the Hejiang granary's vermilion seal.
translations.idiomatic: Junyu had his townsman Bai Zishen draft the edict, but the prose was crude; Juyuan rewrote it and stamped it with the Hejiang granary's vermilion seal.

sentences.zh: 巨源、好義憂事寖泄，遂以二月乙亥未明，好義率其徒入偽宮，巨源持詔乘馬，自稱奉使，入內戶，曦啟戶欲逸，李貴執殺之。

translations.literal: Juyuan and Haoyi feared the affair would gradually leak; thereupon on the yihai day of the second month before dawn, Haoyi led his followers into the false palace; Juyuan held the edict on horseback, calling himself an imperial envoy, entered the inner door; Xi opened the door wishing to flee; Li Gui seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing discovery, they struck before dawn on the yihai day of the second month; Haoyi led his men into the rebel palace while Juyuan rode in bearing the edict and claiming to be an imperial envoy; Xi opened the inner door to flee and Li Gui seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 衛者始拒鬥，聞有詔皆卻。

translations.literal: The guards at first resisted in battle; hearing there was an edict they all fell back.
translations.idiomatic: The guards fought at first, but at the word of an edict they fell back.

sentences.zh: 巨源、好義迎丙宣詔，以曦首徇。

translations.literal: Juyuan and Haoyi welcomed Bing to proclaim the edict, displaying Xi's head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan and Haoyi brought An Bing forth to proclaim the edict and paraded Xi's head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 三軍推丙權四川宣撫使，巨源權參贊軍事。

translations.literal: The three armies pushed Bing as acting Sichuan Pacification Commissioner and Juyuan as acting staff adviser on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The army acclaimed An Bing acting Sichuan pacification commissioner and Yang Juyuan acting military adviser.

sentences.zh: 丙奏功於朝，以巨源第一，詔補承事郎。

translations.literal: Bing reported achievements to the court; ranking Juyuan first, an edict appointed him Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing reported their achievements to court, ranking Yang Juyuan first; an edict appointed him Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 巨源謂丙曰：「曦死，賊膽以破，關外四州為蜀要害，盍乘勢復取。」

translations.literal: Juyuan said to Bing: "Xi is dead—the rebels' courage is broken; the four prefectures beyond the passes are Shu vital points—why not seize the moment to recover them?"
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan told An Bing, "With Xi dead the rebels' nerve is broken. The four prefectures beyond the passes are the keys to Shu—we should seize the moment and take them back.

sentences.zh: 好義亦以為言。

translations.literal: Haoyi also spoke likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi said the same.

sentences.zh: 丙慮軍無見糧，巨源力言四州不取，必有後患，自請為隨軍措置糧運。

translations.literal: Bing worried the army had no grain in sight; Juyuan strongly argued that if the four prefectures were not taken there would surely be later trouble, and volunteered himself to arrange grain transport with the army.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing feared the troops had no supplies in sight; Juyuan insisted that leaving the four prefectures untaken would breed disaster later, and volunteered to manage army grain transport himself.

sentences.zh: 於是分遣好義復西和州，張林、李簡復成州，劉昌國復階州，孫忠銳復散關。

translations.literal: Thereupon they divided forces—Haoyi to recover Xihe Prefecture, Zhang Lin and Li Jian Cheng Prefecture, Liu Changguo Jie Prefecture, Sun Zhongrui San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Forces were sent accordingly: Haoyi to recover Xihe, Zhang Lin and Li Jian to Cheng, Liu Changguo to Jie, and Sun Zhongrui to San Pass.

sentences.zh: 俄詔巨源轉朝奉郎，與通判差譴，兼四川宣撫使司參議官。

translations.literal: Soon an edict transferred Juyuan to Chao Feng Lang, with dispatch equal to a supervisory prefect, and concurrently as advisory officer of the Sichuan Pacification Commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict promoted Juyuan to Chao Feng Lang with supervisory prefect dispatch, and named him advisory officer on the Sichuan pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 丙素惡忠銳，聞忠銳失守散關，檄其還，欲廢之，先命巨源偕邦寧以沔兵二千策應。

translations.literal: Bing had long hated Zhongrui; hearing Zhongrui had lost San Pass, he summoned him back intending to dismiss him, first ordering Juyuan together with Bang Ning to take two thousand Mian troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing had long despised Sun Zhongrui; when he heard San Pass was lost he recalled him to dismiss him, and first sent Juyuan with Bang Ning and two thousand Mian troops to assist.

sentences.zh: 巨源至鳳州，因忠銳出迎，伏壯士於幕後，突出斬之，並其子揆。

translations.literal: Juyuan reached Feng Prefecture; when Zhongrui came out to welcome him, braves were hidden behind the screen—they burst forth and beheaded him, together with his son Kui.
translations.idiomatic: At Feng Prefecture Juyuan welcomed Zhongrui out, then had braves hidden behind the screen rush out and kill him—and his son Kui as well.

sentences.zh: 丙遂以忠銳附偽賀表聞於朝，且待罪。

translations.literal: Bing then sent Zhongrui attached to a false report of congratulation informing the court, and also awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing reported to court with a feigned congratulatory memorial, attaching Zhongrui's case, and awaited punishment himself.

sentences.zh: 先是，獎諭誅叛詔書至沔州，巨源謂人曰：「詔命一字不及巨源，疑有以蔽其功者。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the commendatory edict on executing the rebel reached Mian Prefecture; Juyuan said to others: "The edict's words do not mention Juyuan once—I suspect someone is hiding my achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the edict commending the suppression of the rebellion reached Mian, Juyuan told others, "Not one word of the decree names me—I suspect someone is burying my credit.

sentences.zh: 俄報王喜授節度使，巨源彌不平。

translations.literal: Soon came word that Wang Xi was granted military commissioner; Juyuan grew all the more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Wang Xi had been made military commissioner, and Juyuan's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 時趙彥呐以在夔誅祿禧得州通判，巨源曰：「殺祿禧與通判，殺吳曦亦與通判耶？」

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Yan'a for killing Lu Xi at Kui received prefectural supervisory commission; Juyuan said: "Killing Lu Xi wins supervisory commission—does killing Wu Xi also win supervisory commission?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan'a had just been made supervisory prefect of a prefecture for killing Lu Xi at Kui; Juyuan said, "Slay Lu Xi and you become supervisory prefect—does slaying Wu Xi earn the same prize?

sentences.zh: 以啟謝丙曰：「飛矢以下聊城，深慕魯仲連之高誼；

translations.literal: He opened a letter to thank Bing, saying: "Flying arrows beneath Liaocheng—I deeply admire Lu Zhonglian's lofty righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote An Bing resigning with the words, "When flying arrows fell on Liaocheng, men admired Lu Zhonglian's noble refusal;

sentences.zh: 解印而去彭澤，庶幾陶靖節之清風。」

translations.literal: relinquishing the seal and leaving for Pengze—hoping to approach Tao Jingjie's pure breeze."
translations.idiomatic: relinquishing office and withdrawing to Pengze, in the spirit of Tao Yuanming's integrity."

sentences.zh: 又遣訴功於朝，而從興元都統制彭輅乞書遺韓侂胄，輅陽許而陰以白丙。

translations.literal: He also sent complaints of his achievements to court, and asked Xingyuan metropolitan commander Peng Luo to write a letter to Han Tuozhou; Luo outwardly promised but secretly informed Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He also appealed his service to court and asked Xingyuan metropolitan commander Peng Luo to write Han Tuozhou on his behalf; Luo promised openly but secretly informed An Bing.

sentences.zh: 或言巨源與其徒米福、車彥威謀為亂，丙命喜鞫之，福、彥威皆抵罪。

translations.literal: Someone said Juyuan with his followers Mi Fu and Che Yanwei plotted revolt; Bing ordered Xi to interrogate them—Fu and Yanwei were both convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached An Bing that Juyuan and followers Mi Fu and Che Yanwei were plotting rebellion; he had Wang Xi try them, and both were convicted.

sentences.zh: 正將陳安復告巨源結死士入關，欲焚沔州州治，俟丙出則殺之。

translations.literal: Rectifier Chen Anfu reported that Juyuan had gathered sworn men to enter the passes, intending to burn the Mian prefectural seat, and when Bing came out to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifier Chen Anfu accused Juyuan of rallying death-sworn men to enter the passes, burn the Mian government compound, and kill An Bing when he emerged.

sentences.zh: 丙積前事，因欲去巨源，然未有以發也。

translations.literal: Bing accumulated the earlier matters and thus wished to remove Juyuan, yet had no means to set it off.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing piled up these grievances and wished to be rid of Juyuan, but lacked a pretext.

sentences.zh: 會巨源在鳳州以檄書遺金鳳翔都統使，其辭若用間者，且自稱宣撫副使而以參議官印印之。

translations.literal: It happened that Juyuan at Feng Prefecture sent by dispatch a letter to the Jin Fengxiang metropolitan commander; its wording was like employing spies, and he styled himself deputy pacification commissioner while stamping it with the advisory officer's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Then Juyuan at Feng sent a dispatch to the Jin Fengxiang metropolitan commander with language like a spy stratagem, styled himself deputy pacification commissioner, and sealed it with his advisory officer's stamp.

sentences.zh: 金以檄至丙。

translations.literal: The Jin brought the dispatch to Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin delivered the dispatch to An Bing.

sentences.zh: 巨源方與金戰，敗於長橋，丙乃移書召巨源，巨源疑焉。

translations.literal: Juyuan was then fighting the Jin and was defeated at Chang Bridge; Bing thereupon sent a letter summoning Juyuan—Juyuan was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan was fighting the Jin and lost at Chang Bridge; An Bing summoned him by letter, and Juyuan grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 有梁泉主簿高岳成者，巨源薦為隨軍撥運，來見巨源，贊其歸，巨源信之。

translations.literal: There was Liangquan clerk Gao Yuecheng, whom Juyuan had recommended as army supply allocator; he came to see Juyuan and urged his return—Juyuan believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangquan clerk Gao Yuecheng, whom Juyuan had recommended for army supply duty, came to urge his return—and Juyuan trusted him.

sentences.zh: 時輅已至沔，六月壬申，巨源還幕府，丙密命輅收巨源。

translations.literal: By then Luo had already reached Mian; on the renshen day of the sixth month Juyuan returned to headquarters; Bing secretly ordered Luo to seize Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Luo had already reached Mian; on the renshen day of the sixth month Juyuan returned to headquarters, and An Bing secretly ordered Luo to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 巨源殊不知，以為謁己也，語畢，輅起，巨源送之賓次。

translations.literal: Juyuan knew nothing of it, thinking Luo was calling on him; when the talk ended Luo rose, and Juyuan saw him off to the guest quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan suspected nothing, thinking this a courtesy call; when they finished speaking Luo rose, and Juyuan walked him toward the guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 武士就挽其裾，巨源猶叱之，則已為驅至庭下。

translations.literal: Warriors seized his robe—Juyuan still shouted at them—yet he was already driven to the courtyard below.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors seized his robe; he still shouted them down—but they had already dragged him into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 巨源大呼曰：「我何罪？」

translations.literal: Juyuan cried out: "What is my crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan cried, "What crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 丙隔屏遣人謂之曰：「若為詐稱宣撫副使？」

translations.literal: Bing sent someone through the screen to say: "Why did you falsely claim to be deputy pacification commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: An Bing called through a screen, "Why did you falsely style yourself deputy pacification commissioner?

sentences.zh: 命械送閬州獄。

translations.literal: He ordered him shackled and sent to Lang Prefecture prison.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him shackled and sent to prison at Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巨源曰：「我一時用間，異時必有為我明其事。」

translations.literal: Juyuan said: "I used spies for a moment—in another time someone will surely clarify this affair for me."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "I used a ruse in the moment; someday someone will clear my name.

sentences.zh: 丙餉以肴酒，巨源曰：「一身無愧，死且無憾；

translations.literal: Bing sent him meats and wine; Juyuan said: "My person is without shame—I die without regret;
translations.idiomatic: An Bing sent food and wine; Juyuan said, "I have nothing to regret in dying;

sentences.zh: 惟有妹未嫁，宣撫念之。」

translations.literal: only my younger sister is unmarried—Commissioner, remember her.
translations.idiomatic: only my unmarried sister remains—Commissioner, remember her."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，巨源舟抵大安龍尾灘，將校樊世顯者呼於岸，巨源知將見殺，指其地而語之曰：「此好一片葬地。」

translations.literal: On the guiyou day Juyuan's boat reached Da'an Longwei Beach; adjutant Fan Shixian called from the shore; Juyuan knew he would be killed, pointed at the place and said to him: "This is a fine burial ground."
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day his boat reached Da'an Longwei Beach; adjutant Fan Shixian hailed from the shore; knowing he would die, Juyuan pointed and said, "Fine burial ground here.

sentences.zh: 世顯曰：「安有是？」

translations.literal: Shixian said: "How could there be such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: Shixian said, "Nonsense—

sentences.zh: 舟行數步，謂曰：「宣參久渴，莫進杯酒？」

translations.literal: The boat went a few paces, and he said: "Staff Adviser has long thirsted—will you not offer a cup of wine?"
translations.idiomatic: the boat had gone only a few paces when he said, "Staff Adviser, you must be parched—will you not drink a cup?

sentences.zh: 巨源辭以不飲。

translations.literal: Juyuan declined, saying he did not drink.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan refused, saying he did not drink.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「宣參荷械已久，盍少蘇？」

translations.literal: He also said: "Staff Adviser has borne shackles long—why not rest a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Then, "You have worn fetters long—why not loosen them a little?"

sentences.zh: 巨源未及答，左右遽取利刀斷其頭，不絕者逾寸，遂以巨源自殪聞宣撫司。

translations.literal: Before Juyuan could answer, attendants suddenly took sharp blades and severed his head—not connected by more than an inch—then reported to the pacification office that Juyuan had killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could answer, attendants hacked off his head—barely an inch of flesh still attached—and reported to the pacification office that Juyuan had taken his own life.

sentences.zh: 後數日，丙命瘞之。

translations.literal: Several days later Bing ordered him buried.
translations.idiomatic: Days later An Bing ordered him buried.

sentences.zh: 巨源死，忠義之士為之扼腕，聞者流涕，劍外士人張伯威為文以吊，其辭尤悲切，巨源之屬吏也。

translations.literal: When Juyuan died, men of loyalty and righteousness wrung their wrists for him; hearers wept; Jianwai gentleman Zhang Bowei wrote a mourning text—its words especially mournful—he was Juyuan's subordinate officer.
translations.idiomatic: At Juyuan's death loyal men clenched their fists in grief and listeners wept; Zhang Bowei of the borderlands wrote a mourning piece of exceptional pathos—he had been Juyuan's clerk.

sentences.zh: 李壁在政府，聞之曰：「嘻，巨源其死矣！」

translations.literal: Li Bi in the central government, hearing it, said: "Alas—Juyuan must be dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi at court, hearing the news, said, "Alas—Juyuan is surely dead!

sentences.zh: 丙以人情洶洶，封章求免。

translations.literal: Bing because popular feeling was turbulent submitted sealed memorial asking to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing, facing public outrage, memorialized to resign.

sentences.zh: 楊輔亦謂丙殺巨源必召變，請以劉甲代之。

translations.literal: Yang Fu also said that Bing killing Juyuan would surely summon trouble, and asked that Liu Jia replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu warned that killing Juyuan would bring mutiny and urged replacing An Bing with Liu Jia.

sentences.zh: 初，巨源與好義結官軍，而丙密為反正之計，各未相知，合巨源於好義者李坤辰，而合好義於丙者巨源也。

translations.literal: At the beginning Juyuan and Haoyi had united the official army, while Bing secretly made plans to restore the proper—each did not know the other; Li Kun'an united Juyuan with Haoyi, and Juyuan united Haoyi with Bing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Juyuan and Haoyi had rallied the loyal troops while An Bing had plotted restoration in secret, neither knowing the other's hand—Li Kun'an linked Juyuan to Haoyi, and Juyuan linked Haoyi to An Bing.

sentences.zh: 巨源遺光祖書，述丙酬答之語，鋟梓競傳之，丙已弗樂，浸潤不已，積成此禍。

translations.literal: Juyuan sent a letter to Guangzu describing Bing's replies—block-printed copies competed in circulation; Bing was already displeased—dripping slander without cease piled up into this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan had written to Ye Guangzu quoting An Bing's replies; the letter was printed and passed everywhere; Bing's resentment deepened, slander accumulated, and the disaster grew.

sentences.zh: 成忠郎李珙投匭，獻所作《巨源傳》為之訟冤，朝廷亦念其功，賜廟褒忠，贈寶謨閣待制，官其二子。

translations.literal: Chenzhong Lang Li Qiong submitted to the petition box, presenting his composed "Biography of Juyuan" to plead his wrong; the court also recalled his achievement—granted temple enshrinement as Exalting Loyalty, posthumously made Baomo Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting, and gave offices to his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhong Lang Li Qiong submitted a petition box memorial with his "Biography of Juyuan" to vindicate him; the court remembered his service, granted temple honors as Exalting Loyalty, posthumously made him Baomo Pavilion attendant-in-waiting, and gave offices to his two sons.

sentences.zh: 制置使崔與之請官給其葬，加贈寶謨閣直學士、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Cui Yu with asked official funds for his burial, with added posthumous gift of Baomo Pavilion Academician-in-Waiting and Grand Master of Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Cui Yu with sought state burial funds and added posthumous rank as Baomo Pavilion academician and Grand Master of Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，理宗特賜諡「忠湣」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi Emperor Lizong specially granted the posthumous name "Loyal and Mourned."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 1 (1237) Emperor Lizong granted the posthumous name Zhongmin, "Loyal and Lamented."

sentences.zh: 子：履正，終大理卿、四川制置副使。

translations.literal: Son: Lüzheng, ending as Chief Minister of Justice and Sichuan Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüzheng rose to chief minister of justice and Sichuan pacification vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李好義

translations.literal: Li Haoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Li Haoyi.

sentences.zh: 李好義，下邽人。

translations.literal: Li Haoyi was a native of Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi was from Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 祖師中，建炎間以白丁守華州，積官忠州團練使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shizhong, in the Jianyan era as a commoner defended Hua Prefecture, accumulated office to Zhong Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shizhong, a commoner during the Jianyan era, held Hua Prefecture and rose to Zhong Prefecture defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父定一，興州中軍統制。

translations.literal: His father Dingyi was Xing Prefecture central-army commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dingyi commanded the central army at Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 好義弱冠從軍，善騎射，西邊第一。

translations.literal: Haoyi at twenty sui entered the army, skilled at riding and archery—first on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi took the field in his twenties, unrivaled in horsemanship and archery on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 初以準備將討文州蕃部有功。

translations.literal: At first as preparation officer he attacked Wenzhao tribal groups with achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He first distinguished himself as a preparation officer fighting the Wenzhou tribes.

sentences.zh: 開禧初，韓侂胄開邊，吳曦主師，好義為興州正將，數請出精兵襲金人，曦蓄異謀，不納。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaixi Han Tuozhou opened the frontier; Wu Xi commanded the army; Haoyi was Xing Prefecture rectifier, repeatedly asking to send picked troops to raid the Jin—Xi harbored a separate plot and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaixi, when Han Tuozhou opened the frontier and Wu Xi held command, Haoyi served as rectifier at Xing and repeatedly asked to lead picked troops against the Jin; Xi nursed treason and refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，關外四州俱陷，金人長驅入散關，曦受金人說，以蜀叛。

translations.literal: Before long the four prefectures beyond the passes all fell; the Jin drove deep into San Pass; Xi accepted Jin persuasion and rebelled with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all four border prefectures fell, the Jin swept through San Pass, and Xi, swayed by the Jin, rebelled in Shu.

sentences.zh: 好義自青坊聞變亟歸，與其兄對哭，謀誅之。

translations.literal: Haoyi from Qingfang heard the change and hurried home, wept facing his elder brother, and plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news at Qingfang, Haoyi rushed home, wept with his brother, and plotted Xi's death.

sentences.zh: 會曦遣李貴追殺宣撫程松，貴語其徒曰：「程宣撫朝廷重臣，不可殺。」

translations.literal: It happened that Xi sent Li Gui to pursue and kill Pacification Commissioner Cheng Song; Gui told his followers: "Commissioner Cheng is a weighty court minister—he must not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi sent Li Gui to pursue Pacification Commissioner Cheng Song, Gui told his men, "Commissioner Cheng is a pillar of court—we must not kill him.

sentences.zh: 好義知其赤心，可以所謀告之。

translations.literal: Haoyi knew his loyal heart and could tell him the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi saw his loyal heart and confided the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 貴遂約李彪、張淵、陳立、劉虎、張海等，好義又密結親衛軍黃術、趙亮、吳政等。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon joined Li Biao, Zhang Yuan, Chen Li, Liu Hu, Zhang Hai and others; Haoyi also secretly united personal guard soldiers Huang Shu, Zhao Liang, Wu Zheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Gui rallied Li Biao, Zhang Yuan, Chen Li, Liu Hu, Zhang Hai, and others; Haoyi secretly won over Huang Shu, Zhao Liang, Wu Zheng of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 女弟夫楊君玉亦與知，好義戒言曰：「此事誓死報國，救四蜀生靈，慎毋泄。」

translations.literal: His wife's younger sister's husband Yang Junyu also knew; Haoyi warned, saying: "This affair—we swear death to repay the state and save the four Shu lives—carefully do not leak."
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Yang Junyu joined them; Haoyi warned, "We pledge our lives for the realm and for the people of Shu—tell no one.

sentences.zh: 留其母以質。

translations.literal: He left his mother as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He left his mother behind as pledge of his oath.

sentences.zh: 好義兄弟謀曰：「今日人皆可殺曦，皆可為曦，曦死後，若無威望者鎮撫，恐一變未息，一變復生。」

translations.literal: Haoyi and his brothers plotted, saying: "Today any man can kill Xi or can be Xi; after Xi dies, if there is no man of authority to calm and soothe, I fear one change not ended, another change reborn."
translations.idiomatic: The brothers said, "Anyone might kill Xi today—or serve Xi; after he falls, without a man of stature to steady the realm, one rebellion may end only for another to begin.

sentences.zh: 欲至期立長史安丙以主事，蓋曦嘗授丙偽丞相，而丙託疾不往，故兄弟有是謀也。

translations.literal: They wished when the day came to install Chief Steward An Bing to manage affairs—for Xi had once appointed Bing false chancellor, yet Bing pleaded illness and did not go, so the brothers had this plot.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to install Chief Steward An Bing, whom Xi had named false chancellor but who had pleaded illness and stayed away—that was their design.

sentences.zh: 既而君玉與李坤辰者來，坤辰因言丙亦與合江倉楊巨源陰結忠義欲圖曦。

translations.literal: Then Junyu came with Li Kun'an; Kun'an said Bing also with Hejiang granary Yang Juyuan secretly joined loyal righteousness intending to plot against Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Then Junyu brought Li Kun'an, who said An Bing and Yang Juyuan of the Hejiang granary were already plotting Xi's overthrow.

sentences.zh: 好義遂遣君玉偕坤辰約巨源以報丙。

translations.literal: Haoyi then sent Junyu together with Kun'an to arrange with Juyuan and report to Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi sent Junyu and Kun'an to Juyuan, then to An Bing.

sentences.zh: 丙大喜曰：「非統制李定一之子乎？

translations.literal: Bing greatly rejoiced and said: "Is this not Commander Li Dingyi's son?
translations.idiomatic: An Bing rejoiced. "Are you not Commander Li Dingyi's son?

sentences.zh: 此人既來，斷曦之臂矣。」

translations.literal: This man having come, Xi's arm is severed."
translations.idiomatic: With him here, Xi's right arm is cut off."

sentences.zh: 遂與好義約二月晦舉事，見《巨源傳》。

translations.literal: He then with Haoyi set the last day of the second month to act—see "Biography of Juyuan."
translations.idiomatic: They set the last day of the second month for the strike—see the "Biography of Juyuan."

sentences.zh: 乃約彪、術、貴等七十有四人及士人路良弼、王芾。

translations.literal: He then joined Biao, Shu, Gui and seventy-four others, and gentlemen Lu Liangbi and Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered seventy-four men including Biao, Shu, and Gui, and the scholars Lu Liangbi and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 好義夜饗士，麾眾受甲，與好古、好仁及子姓拜決於家廟，囑妻馬氏曰：「日出無耗，當自為計，死生從此決矣。」

translations.literal: Haoyi at night feasted the soldiers, waved the throng to take armor; with Haogu, Haoren and the clan's younger men he took leave at the family temple; he instructed his wife Lady Ma: "If by sunrise there is no news, make your own plans—life and death are decided from this moment."
translations.idiomatic: That night Haoyi feasted his men and called them to arms; with Haogu, Haoren, and kinsmen he bid farewell at the ancestral shrine and told his wife Lady Ma, "If you hear nothing by sunrise, act for yourself—our lives hang on tonight.

sentences.zh: 馬氏叱之曰：「汝為朝廷誅賊，何以家為？

translations.literal: Lady Ma rebuked him, saying: "You kill the rebel for the court—why speak of family?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ma rebuked him: "You march to slay a traitor for the throne—why trouble yourself over our household?

sentences.zh: 我決不辱李家門戶。」

translations.literal: I will absolutely not dishonor the Li clan gates."
translations.idiomatic: I will not disgrace the Li name.

sentences.zh: 馬氏之母亦曰：「行矣，勉之！

translations.literal: Lady Ma's mother also said: "Go—strive hard!
translations.idiomatic: Her mother said, "Go—and do your utmost!

sentences.zh: 汝兄弟生為壯夫，死為英鬼。」

translations.literal: You brothers living are stalwart men, dead are heroic ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: Live as stalwart men; die as worthy shades."

sentences.zh: 好義喜曰：「婦人女子尚念朝廷不愛性命，我輩當如何？」

translations.literal: Haoyi rejoiced, saying: "Women and girls still think of the court and do not cherish their lives—what ought we men to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi exclaimed, "Even our women hold the throne above their lives—what should we men do?

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍。

translations.literal: The throng all leapt with zeal.
translations.idiomatic: The company answered with a roar.

sentences.zh: 既行，小將祿禕引十卒來助，各以黃帛為號。

translations.literal: Having set out, junior officer Lu Yi led ten soldiers to aid; each used yellow cloth as signal.
translations.idiomatic: As they marched, junior officer Lu Yi brought ten men to help; yellow cloth was their signal.

sentences.zh: 好義誓於眾曰：「入宮妄殺人、掠財物者死。」

translations.literal: Haoyi swore to the crowd: "Entering the palace and killing people at will or plundering goods—death."
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi swore the company to death for any who killed wantonly or looted in the palace.

sentences.zh: 時偽宮門洞開，好義大呼而入曰：「奉朝廷密詔，安長史為宣撫，令我誅反賊，敢抗者夷其族。」

translations.literal: At that time the false palace gates stood wide open; Haoyi shouted entering: "By the court's secret edict Chief Steward An is pacification commissioner; I am ordered to execute the rebel—whoever dares resist, exterminate his clan."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel palace gates stood open; Haoyi burst in shouting, "By secret court edict Chief Steward An is pacification commissioner; we are sent to kill the traitor—resist, and your clan dies.

sentences.zh: 曦護衛千兵皆棄梃而走，遂至偽殿東角小門，入世美堂，近曦寢室。

translations.literal: Xi's thousand palace guards all cast their staffs and fled; they then reached the false hall's eastern corner small gate, entered Shimei Hall, near Xi's bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand guards dropped their staves and fled; they reached the small east gate of the hall, entered Shimei Hall, and closed on Xi's bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 曦聞外哄，倉皇而起，露頂徒跣，開寢戶欲遁，見貴復止，以手捍內戶，貴前爭戶，戶紐折。

translations.literal: Xi heard the outer uproar, rose in panic bare-headed and barefoot, opened the bedchamber door wishing to flee; seeing Gui he stopped again, with his hand blocked the inner door; Gui advanced contending for the door—the door latch broke.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, Xi rose bareheaded and barefoot, opened his chamber to flee, saw Gui, and held the inner door; Gui seized it and the latch snapped.

sentences.zh: 曦走，貴追及，手執其髻，舉刃中曦頰，曦素勇有力，撲貴仆於地不能起。

translations.literal: Xi ran; Gui pursued and seized him by the hair, raised his blade and struck Xi's cheek; Xi was by nature brave and strong—he threw Gui down and he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Xi ran; Gui caught him by the hair and struck his cheek; Xi, brave and powerful, threw Gui down and pinned him.

sentences.zh: 好義急呼王換斧其腰者二，曦負痛手縱，貴起遂斫其首。

translations.literal: Haoyi urgently called Wang Huan to axe his waist twice; Xi in pain released his hands; Gui rose and then hacked off his head.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi called Wang Huan to strike his waist twice; Xi loosed his grip in pain; Gui rose and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 引眾擁曦首出偽宮，亟馳告丙宣詔，軍民拜舞，歡聲動天地，持曦首撫定城中，市不改肆。

translations.literal: Leading the crowd bearing Xi's head out of the false palace, they hurried to tell Bing to proclaim the edict; soldiers and people bowed and danced; joyous voices shook heaven and earth; holding Xi's head they pacified the city—markets changed not their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing Xi's head from the palace, they raced to An Bing to proclaim the edict; soldiers and civilians bowed and cheered till heaven seemed to shake; parading the head they steadied the city, and markets never closed.

sentences.zh: 好義請乘時取關外四州，巨源贊之，丙大喜。

translations.literal: Haoyi asked to seize the moment and take the four prefectures beyond the passes; Juyuan praised it; Bing greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi urged recovering the four border prefectures at once; Juyuan agreed; An Bing was delighted.

sentences.zh: 巨源輔行，王喜忌其能，沮之。

translations.literal: Juyuan accompanied the campaign; Wang Xi envied his ability and obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan marched with him, but Wang Xi, jealous of his talent, undermined the effort.

sentences.zh: 好義曰：「西和乃腹心之地，西和下，則三州可不戰而復矣。

translations.literal: Haoyi said: "Xihe is the heart's core—if Xihe falls, the three prefectures can be recovered without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi said, "Xihe is the heart of the border; take Xihe and the other three may fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 今不圖，後悔無及。

translations.literal: If we do not plan now, regret will not reach us.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and we will repent too late.

sentences.zh: 願得馬步千人，死士二百，齎十日糧可濟。」

translations.literal: I wish to obtain a thousand horse and foot, two hundred death-sworn men—carrying ten days' grain will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Give me a thousand horse and foot, two hundred death-sworn men, and ten days' grain—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 丙從其請，忠義響應，次獨頭嶺，進士王榮仲兄弟率民兵會合夾擊，金人死者蔽路。

translations.literal: Bing followed his request; loyal righteousness answered the call; they next halted at Dutou Ridge; presented scholar Wang Rongzhong and his brothers led militia to join in pincer attack—the Jin dead covered the road.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing agreed; loyal men flocked to the banners; at Dutou Ridge presented scholar Wang Rongzhong and his brothers led militia in a pincer, and Jin dead covered the road.

sentences.zh: 十戰至山砦高堡，七日至西和。

translations.literal: Ten battles to the mountain fort High Castle; on the seventh day they reached Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: After ten fights they reached the mountain redoubt at Gaobao; on the seventh day they stood before Xihe.

sentences.zh: 好義率眾攻城，親犯矢石，人人樂死，以少擊眾，前無留敵。

translations.literal: Haoyi led the crowd assaulting the city, personally braving arrows and stones; every man rejoiced in death; with few striking many, none ahead detained the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi led the assault in person, under arrow and stone; his men fought as if death were joy; few against many, none could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 金西和節使完顏欽奔遁，好義整眾而入，軍民歡呼迎拜，籍府庫以歸於官。

translations.literal: Jin Xihe commissioner Wanyan Qin fled in haste; Haoyi arrayed the troops and entered; soldiers and people shouted welcome and bowed; they registered the treasury to return it to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin commissioner of Xihe, Wanyan Qin, fled; Haoyi entered in good order; soldiers and civilians cheered and bowed; the treasury was inventoried for the state.

sentences.zh: 好義初欲乘勝徑取秦、隴以牽制淮寇，而宣撫司令謹守故疆，不得侵越，士氣皆沮。

translations.literal: Haoyi at first wished to ride victory straight to take Qin and Long to tie down Huai bandits, but the pacification commission ordered strict defense of the old borders—no crossing permitted—all morale was dejected.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi had meant to press on toward Qin and Long and draw off the Huai enemy, but the pacification commissioner ordered the old border held inviolate; morale sank.

sentences.zh: 好義以中軍統制知西和州，卒。

translations.literal: Haoyi as central-army commander governed Xihe Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyi governed Xihe as central-army commander, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 丙以勞績上於朝，特贈檢校少保，仍給田以贍其家。

translations.literal: Bing reported his labors and achievements to court; he was specially posthumously made Acting Junior Guardian, and still granted fields to support his family.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing reported his service to court; he was posthumously made acting Junior Guardian, and granted fields to support his household.

sentences.zh: 後吳獵為請諡曰「忠壯」。

translations.literal: Later Wu Lie sought the posthumous name "Loyal and Stalwart."
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Lie secured the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, "Loyal and Stout."

sentences.zh: 好義喜誦《孟子》及《左傳》，以為終身行此足矣。

translations.literal: Haoyi delighted in reciting the Mencius and the Zuozhuan, holding that a lifetime walking these suffices.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Mencius and the Zuo Commentary and held that to live by them was enough for a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 誅曦時，惟幼子植留家。

translations.literal: When Xi was executed, only his youngest son Zhi remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: When they killed Xi, only his youngest son Zhi was left at home.

sentences.zh: 迄事，人爭冒功賞，君玉欲注植名，好義指心曰：「惟此物不可欺。」

translations.literal: When the affair was done, men scrambled to claim merit rewards; Junyu wished to enter Zhi's name; Haoyi pointed to his heart and said: "Only this thing cannot be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: When all was over, men scrambled to claim credit; Junyu wanted to list Zhi among the rewarded, but Haoyi touched his heart and said, "This alone cannot be lied to."

sentences.zh: 曦既誅，好義集於丙家，王喜後至，心懷邪謀，欲刃好義，丙力救解，然日以殺好義為心。

translations.literal: After Xi was executed, Haoyi gathered at Bing's house; Wang Xi arrived later, harboring evil designs, wishing to blade Haoyi; Bing exerted himself to rescue and release him, yet day by day took killing Haoyi to heart.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Xi was killed, Haoyi met at An Bing's house; Wang Xi arrived later with murder in mind and tried to stab Haoyi, but Bing forcibly intervened—though Xi thereafter nursed a daily resolve to kill him.

sentences.zh: 及好義守西和，喜遣其死黨劉昌國聽節制，好義與之酬酢，歡飲達旦，好義心腹暴痛洞瀉，而昌國遁矣。

translations.literal: When Haoyi held Xihe, Xi sent his death-bound follower Liu Changguo to accept his command; Haoyi exchanged toasts with him, drinking merrily until dawn; Haoyi's belly suddenly ached violently with flux, and Changguo vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When Haoyi was defending Xihe, Xi sent his sworn henchman Liu Changguo under his command; Haoyi drank with him until dawn, then suffered violent cramping and dysentery—while Changguo slipped away.

sentences.zh: 既殮，口鼻爪指皆青黑，居民莫不冤之，號慟如私親，摧鋒一軍幾至於變。

translations.literal: After encoffining, mouth, nose, claws, and fingers were all blue-black; residents all deemed it injustice, wailing as for kin; the Cuifeng army nearly mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral his mouth, nose, nails, and fingers were all blue-black; the people believed he had been wronged and mourned him as kin; the Cuifeng regiment nearly rose in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 既而昌國白日見好義持刃刺之，驚怖仆地，疽發而殂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Changguo by day saw Haoyi holding a blade stabbing him; terrified he fell prostrate; gangrene broke out and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Changguo saw Haoyi in broad daylight, blade in hand, stabbing at him; he collapsed in terror, gangrene set in, and he died.

sentences.zh: 喜，曦大將也，貪淫狠愎，誅曦之日不肯拜詔，遣其徒入偽宮虜掠殆盡，又取曦姬妾數人。

translations.literal: Xi was a great general of Xi, greedy, lecherous, cruel, and obstinate; on the day Xi was executed he refused to bow to the edict, sent his followers into the false palace to plunder nearly everything, and also took several of Xi's concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi had been one of Wu Xi's chief generals—greedy, lecherous, cruel, and obstinate. On the day Xi was killed he refused to acknowledge the edict, sent his men to loot the rebel palace bare, and took several of Xi's concubines for himself.

sentences.zh: 其後欲戕好義為曦復仇，丙不能止，便宜處以節度使知興州，而恨猶未已。

translations.literal: Afterward he wished to harm Haoyi to avenge Xi; Bing could not stop him and on emergency authority made him military commissioner and prefect of Xingzhou, yet hatred was still not ended.
translations.idiomatic: He later sought to kill Haoyi to avenge Wu Xi; Bing could not restrain him and on emergency authority appointed him military commissioner of Xingzhou, yet his hatred was still not spent.

sentences.zh: 嘗出兵於船柵嶺，鋒未及交，棄軍先遁，金人遂由黑谷長驅入境。

translations.literal: Once he led troops out at Boat-Palisade Ridge; before the vanguards met he abandoned the army and fled first; the Jin then drove deep into the territory through Black Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Once he marched to Boat-Palisade Ridge but fled before the lines engaged, allowing the Jin to pour through Black Valley deep into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮喜為變，授節度使移荊鄂都統制而死。

translations.literal: The court feared Xi would rebel, granted him military commissioner and transferred him to Jing-E commander-in-chief, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he might rebel, the court made him military commissioner and transferred him to commander-in-chief of Jing-E, where he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳敏善守，畢再遇善戰。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Chen Min excelled at defense, Bi Zaiyu at combat.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: Chen Min excelled at defense, Bi Zaiyu at offensive warfare.

sentences.zh: 張詔出使不辱國，為將得士心，趙汝愚薦為武興帥，以其才足以制曦也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao on embassy did not disgrace the state; as general he won the troops' hearts; Zhao Ruyu recommended him as Wuxing commander, judging his talent sufficient to control Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao on embassy brought no shame on the state; as a commander he won his soldiers' loyalty; Zhao Ruyu had recommended him for Wuxing precisely because his talent could have checked Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 曦之畔，向非安丙、楊巨源、李好義之謀，西方之憂莫大焉。

translations.literal: Xi's rebellion—had it not been for the plots of An Bing, Yang Juyuan, and Li Haoyi—the troubles of the west would have been beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for the conspiracy of An Bing, Yang Juyuan, and Li Haoyi, Wu Xi's rebellion would have brought immeasurable calamity to the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 然丙卒以是殺巨源，何其冒疾而殘賊也？

translations.literal: Yet Bing in the end for this killed Juyuan—how rash in illness and cruel toward the loyal?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bing ultimately killed Juyuan for it—how rash his jealousy and how cruel toward a man who had saved the realm?

sentences.zh: 李好義失於周防，竟為王喜所圖。

translations.literal: Li Haoyi failed in circumspect defense and in the end was plotted against by Wang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi failed to guard against treachery and was ultimately destroyed by Wang Xi.

sentences.zh: 宋知喜為曦黨，既不能罪，又以節鎮賞之，幾何而不為唐末之姑息以成藩鎮之禍乎？

translations.literal: Song knew Xi was a partisan of Xi, yet could neither punish him nor but reward him with a frontier command—how was this not the late-Tang indulgence that bred the calamity of regional warlords?
translations.idiomatic: The Song court knew Wang Xi was Wu Xi's partisan, yet neither punished him nor withheld a frontier command—how was this not the late-Tang policy of appeasement that bred the warlord catastrophe?
